Its flagship product, Simi, turns prompts, documents, and AI-generated answers into whiteboard-style teaching videos in seconds, handling script writing, illustration, animation, and narration automatically, for durations from one minute to an hour and in over 80 languages. The company targets training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and educational use cases, with the stated goal of making video the default interface for AI communication. Lamina exposes Simi to agents through a public remote MCP server at https://api.laminalabs.ai/mcp, secured by an OAuth 2.1-style authorization server with PKCE, dynamic client registration, and job-scoped access tokens.

providers.name: University of Antwerp
providers.description: The University of Antwerp (Universiteit Antwerpen) is a public research university in Antwerp, Belgium, ranked #267 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer and API footprint is centered on its library and scholarly infrastructure: the university library's software department, Anet, builds the open-source Brocade library management system and publishes code via the anet-be GitHub organization. The Institutional Repository University of Antwerp (IRUA) exposes scholarly metadata through a standards-based OAI-PMH interface. The university does not operate a general-purpose commercial developer portal; administrative, student-information, and identity systems are gated behind institutional affiliation rather than offered as public self-service APIs.

providers.name: University of Indonesia
providers.description: University of Indonesia (Universitas Indonesia, UI) is a public research university based in Depok and Salemba, Jakarta, ranked #206 in the QS World University Rankings 2025 and the highest-ranked university in Indonesia. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is limited: UI Scholars Hub, the institutional research repository hosted on the Digital Commons (bepress) platform, exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata interface for harvesting scholarly works, and the campus-wide Single Sign-On runs on CAS (Central Authentication Service). No public, self-service developer portal with documented REST endpoints or API keys was found; academic, library, and identity systems are gated behind institutional credentials.

providers.name: Gadjah Mada University
providers.description: Gadjah Mada University (Universitas Gadjah Mada, UGM) is a public research university in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, and is ranked #239 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-consumable developer footprint is limited: the institutional repository (EPrints "repository civitas UGM") exposes a working OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata endpoint for harvesting scholarly output, and the university operates a centralized CAS single sign-on service. Most academic and administrative systems (SIMASTER, admissions) sit behind authentication, and there is no public, documented developer portal.

providers.name: Qatar University
providers.description: Qatar University is the national public research university of the State of Qatar, located in Doha, and ranked #122 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is concentrated in QSpace, the university's institutional repository running on DSpace 7.6, which exposes a public OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting endpoint and a public DSpace REST/HAL API for scholarly output and academic records. Most other institutional systems (Self-Service Banner SIS, library discovery, SSO/MFA) are gated behind authentication and do not publish open developer documentation.

providers.name: Tohoku University
providers.description: Tohoku University is a national research university in Sendai, Japan, founded in 1907 and ranked #107 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly infrastructure rather than a central developer portal: the TOUR (TOhoku University Repository) institutional repository runs on NII's JAIRO Cloud (WEKO3) and exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint for metadata harvesting. The library also operates a public OPAC. No central, self-service API developer portal, open-data platform, or SSO/OAuth client-registration program was found publicly documented; most research-code APIs live in individual lab GitHub organizations.

providers.name: University of Lisbon
providers.description: The University of Lisbon (Universidade de Lisboa, ULisboa) is Portugal's largest public university, based in Lisbon, and is ranked #260 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer/API footprint is decentralized across its schools and services rather than offered through a single institutional developer portal. The most prominent programmable interfaces are the FenixEdu academic API operated by Instituto Superior Tecnico (tecnico.ulisboa.pt) and the OAI-PMH metadata interface of the DSpace institutional repository (repositorio.ulisboa.pt). The ULisboa GitHub organization publishes open-source Java libraries focused on Erasmus Without Paper (EWP) data exchange. There is no single self-service commercial API program; most interfaces are open metadata endpoints or affiliation-gated systems.

providers.name: University of Liverpool
providers.description: The University of Liverpool is a public research university in Liverpool, United Kingdom, a founding member of the Russell Group, ranked #165 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly and research-data infrastructure rather than a unified developer portal: the EPrints-based University of Liverpool Repository and the DataCat research data catalogue both expose live OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interfaces. No general-purpose public API developer portal, course/timetable API, or self-service API key program was found to be publicly documented at the time of review; most institutional systems (SSO/IdP, student administration, mobile backends) sit behind authentication and are not publicly cataloged.

providers.name: Citation File Format
providers.description: The Citation File Format (CFF) is a human- and machine-readable YAML schema for providing citation metadata for software and datasets in source code repositories. A CITATION.cff file at the root of a repository declares authors, version, DOI, release date, and reference metadata, enabling consistent academic attribution across publishing and discovery platforms. CFF is governed as an open community standard with a published JSON Schema, a guide, and a maintained schema repository on GitHub. Native integrations include GitHub citation display, Zenodo software publishing, and the Zotero browser plugin. Tooling includes cffinit for authoring, cffconvert for conversion to BibTeX/RIS/CodeMeta/EndNote formats, and the cff-validator GitHub Action for CI validation. The current schema version is 1.2.0.

providers.name: TrueCoach
providers.description: TrueCoach is a personal-training and remote-coaching platform for strength coaches, personal trainers, and physical therapists to deliver workouts online and train clients remotely. Started as Fitbot out of Techstars Boulder and now an Xplor Technologies brand, it offers a web app plus iOS and Android client apps with program and workout builders, a video exercise library, nutrition tracking, wearables data, Stripe-powered payments, a MyFitnessPal integration, and a Zapier connector — but publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: DeepHow
providers.description: DeepHow is an enterprise Physical AI platform that helps industrial companies capture, verify, and optimize operational knowledge across manufacturing, pharmaceutical, and electronics assembly environments. It turns expert know-how into searchable digital workflows, uses vision AI for live standard-operating-procedure (SOP) verification and on-demand visual inspection, and applies time-and-motion AI for task analysis and operator training and enablement. DeepHow is used by 100+ enterprises including Stanley Black & Decker, Anheuser-Busch InBev, Foxconn, and GSK. It is backed by Sierra Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: Chulalongkorn University
providers.description: Chulalongkorn University is Thailand's oldest and a leading public research university, located in Bangkok and ranked #229 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer/API footprint is limited and largely oriented toward identity and scholarly content: a campus single sign-on (Chula SSO) authentication API for student/staff login, an institutional repository (CUIR / Chula Digiverse, built on DSpace) exposing OAI-PMH and REST interfaces, and a staff-only central data exchange (CU Data Gateway) that offers an online API mode. There is no unified, openly documented public developer portal; access to most services is gated to university personnel or granted on request.

providers.name: Ghent University
providers.description: Ghent University (Universiteit Gent, UGent) is a major public research university in Ghent, Belgium, ranked #169 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer footprint centers on the Ghent University Library: the Academic Bibliography (biblio.ugent.be) exposes a documented REST search API plus OAI-PMH, SRU, unAPI and bulk data dumps under an ODbL license, and the library catalog (lib.ugent.be) offers OAI-PMH, SRU, IIIF and OpenSearch interfaces. The university maintains official GitHub organizations (ugent, ugent-library), and the student computer-science group Zeus WPI publishes the open Hydra Resto API for student-restaurant menu data. There is no single centralized, gateway-style institutional developer portal; APIs are documented per service.

providers.name: University of Florida
providers.description: The University of Florida (UF) is a public land-grant research university in Gainesville, Florida, United States, and ranks #215 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UF does not operate a single centralized public developer portal, but several public and community-documented HTTP/JSON data endpoints exist across its web properties: a Schedule of Courses (SOC) API served from one.ufl.edu, campus map JSON datasets, and the UF Digital Collections (UFDC) which exposes metadata via OAI-PMH and RSS. Most institutional APIs (identity, SIS, enterprise integrations) are gated behind UFIT authentication and are not publicly documented.

providers.name: HTTPX
providers.description: HTTPX is a fully featured HTTP client for Python 3 with sync and async APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support. It is broadly compatible with the popular requests library while adding modern features such as strict timeouts, type annotations, direct WSGI and ASGI transport, SSL verification, cookie persistence, proxy support, and multipart uploads.

providers.name: Opensesame
providers.description: OpenSesame is an online learning course marketplace founded in 2002 and headquartered in Portland, Oregon. It offers 60,000+ pre-vetted training courses in 70+ languages spanning compliance, business skills, safety, technology, leadership, and industry-specific topics, and delivers them into an organization's existing learning management system through a patented one-click curation integration with automatic daily metadata sync and xAPI progress reporting. OpenSesame is a portfolio company of Partech and maintains a public trust center with SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and GDPR posture.

providers.name: University of Wollongong
providers.description: The University of Wollongong (UOW) is a public research university based in Wollongong, New South Wales, Australia, ranked #167 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UOW does not operate a public, self-service developer portal. Its confirmed machine-readable footprint is built on third-party platforms: the Research Online institutional repository runs on bepress Digital Commons and exposes an OAI-PMH metadata interface, while the UOW Library runs on the Ex Libris Alma/Primo platform whose REST APIs are documented through the Ex Libris Developer Network. UOW IT Services also maintains a small public GitHub organization. Most institutional systems (student administration, identity) are gated behind authentication and not publicly documented.

providers.name: Expected Parrot
providers.description: Expected Parrot is a research-technology company building tools for AI-powered social science. Its open-source Python library EDSL (Expected Parrot Domain-Specific Language) lets researchers design, conduct, and analyze surveys and experiments in which large language models power simulated AI agents that answer questions, alongside or in place of human respondents. The Expected Parrot platform adds remote inference across many model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, and more) via a single Expected Parrot API key, plus cloud storage, sharing, and collaboration for surveys, agents, scenarios, and results. It is used for market research, data labeling, digital twins, synthetic-user UX studies, and reproducible computational social science.

providers.name: Hokkaido University
providers.description: Hokkaido University (北海道大学) is a national research university in Sapporo, Japan, founded in 1876 as Sapporo Agricultural College and ranked #173 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates 12 undergraduate schools, 21 graduate schools, and numerous research institutes. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is limited and centered on scholarly infrastructure: the HUSCAP institutional repository (Hokkaido University Collection of Scholarly and Academic Papers) and public XML sitemaps. The university does not publish a dedicated developer portal or documented public REST API; most institutional systems (ELMS LMS, syllabus search, researcher directory) are web UIs without documented programmatic access.

providers.name: Massey University
providers.description: Massey University is a public research university in New Zealand with campuses in Palmerston North, Wellington, and Auckland, ranked #239 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable footprint is centered on Massey Research Online (MRO), the institutional repository built on DSpace 8.3, which exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata-harvesting interface and a HAL/JSON DSpace REST API. The university's former M-API WebService is now a legacy service and is no longer available. There is no broadly published general-purpose developer portal; most institutional API access (the historical M-API) was gated behind an ITS Service Desk developer-key request.

providers.name: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia
providers.description: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), The National University of Malaysia, is a public research university in Bangi, Selangor, ranked #138 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is concentrated in scholarly-communication infrastructure operated by the Perpustakaan Tun Seri Lanang (UKM Library): a DSpace-based UKM Learning and Research Repository and an EPrints-based UKM Journal Article Repository, both of which expose standards-based OAI-PMH harvesting interfaces. UKM does not publish a general-purpose developer portal; student and staff online services are gated behind institutional single sign-on and are not openly documented.

providers.name: University of Campinas
providers.description: The University of Campinas (Universidade Estadual de Campinas, Unicamp) is a public research university in Campinas, São Paulo, Brazil, ranked #232 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its most visible public, machine-readable API footprint is REDU, the Unicamp Research Data Repository, which runs on the open-source Dataverse 6.0 platform and exposes a documented Native/Search API and an OAI-PMH metadata endpoint. Institutional data products are otherwise delivered through dashboards and gated portals (EDAT / dados.unicamp.br) and library discovery systems rather than a unified public developer portal.

providers.name: Crimson Education
providers.description: Crimson Education is a multinational university admissions consultancy founded in Auckland, New Zealand in 2013 by Jamie Beaton, Fangzhou Jiang and Sharndre Kushor. It provides college-prep and admissions consulting for US, UK, EU and Australian universities, graduate and medical school admissions support, curriculum tutoring and extracurricular mentoring, and operates the Crimson Global Academy online high school alongside brands including MedView, Crimson MBA and Unfiltered. Its student and mentor experience runs on the Crimson App, whose backend REST and GraphQL surface is reached through a first-party TypeScript SDK published on npm as @crimson-education/sdk.

providers.name: Tonal
providers.description: Tonal is a connected fitness company founded in 2013 by Aly Orady and headquartered in San Francisco, best known for its wall-mounted smart home gym that uses digital weight (electromagnetic resistance) and AI-powered coaching to deliver personalized strength training. The Tonal 2 hardware pairs with a subscription membership offering adaptive weight adjustment, science-backed workout programs, live and on-demand classes, and progress tracking. Tonal publishes no first-party developer API, but its Shopify-hosted storefront exposes an agent-commerce surface: an llms.txt, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and an MCP endpoint for agent-driven shopping.

providers.name: Blue J
providers.description: Blue J is an AI-powered tax research platform that delivers defensible, source-backed answers to complex tax questions in seconds, drawing on primary law plus Tax Notes and IBFD content. Built for tax professionals, the platform supports advisory, compliance, tax writing, and training workflows, and is trusted by 4,000+ firms including Crowe, RSM, and Larson. Blue J is a SaaS product accessed through its web application at app.askbluej.com; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or MCP server. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Blue J's own public website, security, pricing, and trust-center pages.

providers.name: Khalifa University
providers.description: Khalifa University of Science and Technology is a research-intensive university in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, ranked #202 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates colleges of Engineering and Physical Sciences, Computing and Mathematical Sciences, and Medicine and Health Sciences, along with multiple research centers. No central public, documented developer or API program was found; student and administrative systems (KU Connect portal, Banner registration, e-Learn, library discovery) are gated behind institutional authentication. The only confirmed public code footprint is the GitHub organization of its Center for Autonomous Robotic Systems (KUCARS), which publishes open-source robotics research repositories rather than a managed, documented API.

providers.name: Sapienza University of Rome
providers.description: Sapienza University of Rome (Sapienza Università di Roma) is Italy's largest university and ranked #132 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public machine-readable footprint is centered on research and library data rather than a unified developer portal: the IRIS institutional research catalogue exposes a DSpace OAI-PMH endpoint for harvesting research metadata, and the Sapienza Library System (Sistema Bibliotecario Sapienza) publishes open data and linked data following the 5-star open data model. There is no single official, documented public REST API gateway; identity is federated via the Italian IDEM Shibboleth/SAML federation. A GitHub organization carrying the Sapienza name exists but hosts research and coursework projects rather than official platform APIs.

providers.name: Sungkyunkwan University
providers.description: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) is a private research university in Seoul and Suwon, South Korea, with roots dating to 1398, and is ranked #123 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its digital footprint centers on the Kingo Portal single sign-on environment, the iCampus learning system, the university library, and the KINGO-M mobile app. As of this review SKKU publishes no public, documented developer API or open-data portal; integration and identity services (Kingo SSO, eduroam) are gated to enrolled students, faculty, and staff. Public software activity exists mainly through research-lab and student developer-community GitHub organizations rather than a central institutional developer program.

providers.name: University of Gothenburg
providers.description: The University of Gothenburg (Göteborgs universitet) is a public research university in Sweden, founded in 1891, with roughly 37,000 students and 6,000 employees, and ranked #194 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-centric rather than a unified developer program: the Gothenburg University Library operates the GUPEA institutional repository (DSpace) which exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata interface, and the Quality of Government (QoG) Institute publishes open-access datasets via downloads and a Data Finder tool. The university does not appear to operate a central, documented developer portal with public REST API keys; affiliated technical work is distributed across departmental GitHub organizations.

providers.name: Vanderbilt University
providers.description: Vanderbilt University is a private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, ranked #248 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer/API footprint is limited and largely gated: Vanderbilt IT (VUIT) offers API integration and management services to faculty and staff, fronted by an Azure API Management developer portal that does not resolve for the general public (internal/network-gated). The Jean and Alexander Heard Libraries maintain an open GitHub presence (linked data, semantic web, institutional repository tooling) and run an Ex Libris Alma/Primo library platform that supports standard OAI-PMH and discovery APIs. No official, publicly documented, self-service Vanderbilt API was confirmed during review.

providers.name: Scott Foresman
providers.description: Scott Foresman was a leading elementary educational publisher for PreK through Grade 6 across all subject areas. Founded in 1896, the company became part of Pearson PLC in 1996. In 2019, Pearson spun off its U.S.-based K-12 courseware business, which was rebranded as Savvas Learning Company in 2020. Scott Foresman's iconic educational content — including the "Dick and Jane" reading series and basal reading programs — now lives under the Savvas Learning brand. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Literati
providers.description: Literati is an Austin, Texas based children's book company founded by Jessica Ewing that operates three connected consumer and school businesses: personalized monthly Book Clubs for Kids that ship five curated books matched to a child's reading level and interests starting at $11.95 per month, Clubs for Classrooms for teachers, and a school book fair business (in-person and online) run through the OpenBook coordinator dashboard at openbook.literati.com and the year-round Literati Store, which returns a share of proceeds to participating schools. The company draws on 150+ publishers, combines expert curation with data science to personalize book selection, and reports more than one million books donated to Title I schools and underserved communities since 2019. Literati publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; its public technical surface is limited to consumer and school-facing web applications, iOS and Android apps, and an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-reporting contact.

providers.name: Yonsei University
providers.description: Yonsei University (연세대학교) is a private research university in Seoul, South Korea, founded in 1885 and one of the "SKY" institutions. Its programmable footprint is small, and most of what previously appeared under its name was not its own engineering: the Yonsei Research Information portal at yonsei.elsevierpure.com is an Elsevier Pure (CRIS) tenancy whose OpenAPI is authored by Elsevier — info.title "Pure API", contact pure-support@elsevier.com — and whose data endpoints and OAI-PMH feed both return HTTP 401 to the public. That relationship is recorded here as a tenant surface; the contract itself belongs to Elsevier and has been removed from this repo. What Yonsei genuinely operates is narrower and more interesting: a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider on its own domain (kafe.yonsei.ac.kr) registered in the Korean Access FEderation and exported to eduGAIN with the scope yonsei.ac.kr and a Sirtfi declaration; a DSpace 5.5 medical-library repository (YUHSpace) at ir.ymlib.yonsei.ac.kr serving public RSS 2.0 and Atom 1.0 feeds from behind a JavaScript bot challenge, with no OAI-PMH deployed; and a members-only Yonsei Data Portal at data.yonsei.ac.kr that ships no public API. There is no central developer portal, no institution-operated REST API, and no official institutional GitHub organization — the only GitHub presence is GDGoC Yonsei, a student Google Developer Group. The institutional AI posture is a governance document, not an API, and it exists only on the Korean surface.

providers.name: Infleqtion
providers.description: Infleqtion is a Louisville/Boulder, Colorado quantum-technology company — formerly ColdQuanta — that builds neutral-atom quantum computers, precision atomic clocks, and quantum sensors for governments, corporations, and research institutions. Its computing portfolio spans Sqale (a full-stack, fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum computer), Quantum Cores (ready-to-use neutral-atom systems for laboratories), and Superstaq, an open-source quantum software platform with proprietary cross-layer optimization that compiles Qiskit, Cirq, and OpenQASM circuits down to hardware-native operations and routes them across heterogeneous quantum backends. Infleqtion's sensing portfolio includes the Tiqker optical atomic clock, Quantum Spectrum (Rydberg atomic spectrum sensing), and inertial sensors for GPS-denied positioning. The company was founded in 2007 as ColdQuanta, rebranded to Infleqtion in November 2022 after absorbing the Super.tech quantum-software acquisition, and became Infleqtion, Inc. (NASDAQ: INFQ) in January 2026. Superstaq (qiskit-superstaq, cirq-superstaq, general-superstaq) is the only developer-facing public surface; the hardware and sensing businesses are sold via direct engagement and government contracts rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Retrofit
providers.description: Retrofit is a type-safe HTTP client for Android and the JVM (Java and Kotlin) built by Square, turning HTTP API interfaces into callable Java objects with annotation-based configuration and pluggable serialization. Retrofit is built on top of OkHttp and supports synchronous/asynchronous execution, JSON/XML/Protobuf converters, RxJava adapters, and Kotlin coroutines. Current stable version is 3.0.0.

providers.name: Sunlight
providers.description: Sunlight is an educational-spending platform that lets organizations fund learning for their people. Administrators create groups, invite registered or unregistered members, allocate a per-user education budget ("sunlight"), and let members place orders for courses, books and subscriptions from providers such as Amazon and Platzi, while an activity feed tracks what members join and buy. Its REST API is built on the JSON:API specification (media type application/vnd.api+json) with Bearer-token authentication, and exposes groups, group membership and invitations, per-user credit/budget transactions, orders, and activities. Sunlight was backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Autonomous University of Barcelona
providers.description: The Autonomous University of Barcelona (Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, UAB) is a public research university in Bellaterra, near Barcelona, Spain, founded in 1968 and ranked #175 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UAB's public, machine-accessible footprint centers on its open scholarly infrastructure rather than a formal developer portal: the Dipòsit Digital de Documents (DDD), the institutional repository built on the Invenio platform, exposes an OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata endpoint and is OpenAIRE-compliant. Research data is published through the Catalan consortium (CSUC) federated research data repository. No dedicated, publicly documented UAB developer/API program or official institutional GitHub organization was confirmed; student-facing academic services (SIA) are gated login portals without public API documentation.

providers.name: Lecturio
providers.description: Lecturio is a medical and nursing education technology company headquartered in Leipzig, Germany (Lecturio GmbH), serving more than 500,000 learners and educators across 175+ countries. The platform combines video lectures, concept pages, spaced-repetition quizzes, and AI-tutored question banks covering 20+ preclinical and clinical subjects, with exam preparation for USMLE, NBME, COMLEX, MCAT, PANCE, NCLEX-RN, and international licensure exams such as the Saudi SNLE. Alongside the direct-to-student Lecturio Medical and Lecturio Nursing products, the company sells institutional platforms to medical schools, nursing schools, hospitals, and residency programs under the Healer (clinical reasoning), SimTutor (simulation authoring), and SIMTICS (procedural simulation) brands. Lecturio publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its public machine-readable surface consists of an RFC 9116 security.txt, a self-managed vulnerability disclosure policy, and a Rank Math generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Novakid
providers.description: Novakid is an online English language school for children aged roughly 4-12, founded in 2017 by Max Azarov and Dmitry Malin, incorporated in the United States and operating as a fully remote company with a head office in London. It delivers 25-minute one-to-one and small-group video lessons with native and near-native speaking teachers through a proprietary gamified virtual classroom, on a curriculum aligned to the CEFR framework, and sells directly to parents as a subscription across Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia. Novakid is a direct-to-consumer education product: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its production API host serves a blanket robots.txt disallow.

providers.name: UCSI University
providers.description: UCSI University is a private, multi-campus university in Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur, Terengganu and Sarawak) ranked #265 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates student-facing digital services including a student portal and mobile apps and runs a Koha-based library catalog, but UCSI does not publish a public developer portal or documented, openly accessible APIs. The systems that exist (portal, mobile-app backends, identity) are gated behind authentication and a web application firewall, so no public API endpoints could be confirmed during this review.

providers.name: Covalent
providers.description: Covalent (Covalent Networks) is a workforce operations software company for industrial manufacturing teams in the aerospace & defense and automotive sectors, with Fortune 500 manufacturing clients including Boeing. Its platform connects workforce skills, task execution and production data to digitize on-the-job training, capability and skills management, intelligent work allocation, workforce scheduling, and workflow automation with audit reporting, replacing paper-based shop-floor processes. Covalent exposes a GraphQL API and bidirectional integrations to move workforce, skills and production data across enterprise systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, UKG, Microsoft, and LMS/ERP/MES platforms. API access is authenticated with AWS Cognito (OAuth2/OIDC with MFA) and provisioned per tenant. The company is headquartered in Boston, MA and is backed by Felicis.

providers.name: edX
providers.description: edX is an online learning platform now operated by 2U; the underlying Open edX software is open source. Open edX exposes a comprehensive REST API surface (Enrollment, Courses, Users, Catalog, Discussion, Grades, LTI, Enterprise) and hosts a public API at api.edx.org for partners.

providers.name: Podium Education
providers.description: Podium Education is an Austin, Texas experiential-learning and career platform founded in 2018 that partners with colleges, universities and employers to close the college-to-career gap. Its flagship program, The Global Career Accelerator, is a credit-bearing, financial-aid and Pell-eligible online field experience in which undergraduates work on real brand projects in data analytics, web development, digital marketing and tech operations alongside peers in other countries, earning certificates and minors through their own institution. Podium delivers the program on its own platform stack — a hosted Canvas LMS estate and a student application at globalcareeraccelerator.org — sold to universities as a partnership rather than as software, and it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: TIAA-CREF
providers.description: TIAA (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America, formerly TIAA-CREF) is a Fortune 100 leading provider of financial services for people in the academic, research, medical, cultural, and government fields. With $1.5 trillion in assets under management, TIAA serves over 4.7 million individual customers and more than 12,000 institutional clients. Founded in 1918, TIAA invented the variable annuity in 1952 via the College Retirement Equities Fund (CREF) and is known for its TIAA Traditional fixed annuity and lifetime income solutions. TIAA wholly owns Nuveen Investments, a major institutional asset management firm. TIAA serves primarily non-profit organizations, universities, hospitals, and government entities with retirement plans including 403(b), 457(b), and 401(k) plans.

providers.name: AMBOSS
providers.description: AMBOSS is a Berlin-based (AMBOSS SE) digital medical knowledge platform used by medical students, physicians, educators, and healthcare institutions worldwide. It combines a physician-authored medical library, exam-style Qbanks with AI-powered analytics, and a point-of-care clinical reference tool, plus AI features (LiSA) for evidence-based clinical decision support. AMBOSS sells consumer memberships and institutional licenses to medical schools, residency programs, and hospitals. It is a Partech portfolio company. This profile was enriched from AMBOSS' public web and security surface; the medical platform publishes no public developer API (its amboss-mededu GitHub org hosts internal tooling), so this repo carries identity and security artifacts rather than API specifications.

providers.name: memrise
providers.description: Memrise is a language-learning app founded in 2010 and headquartered in London, UK, trusted by 80 million learners across iOS, Android, and web. It is built around real native-speaker video, goal-based specialised courses (exams, work, relationships, travel), a spaced-repetition memory-science engine created by co-founder and Princeton neuroscientist Greg Detre, and AI conversation practice. Memrise offers courses in 149+ languages and has been profitable since 2016. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. Memrise is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and machine-readable (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: RMIT University
providers.description: RMIT University is a public research university in Melbourne, Australia, specializing in technology, design and enterprise, and ranked #123 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. RMIT does not operate a centralized, publicly documented developer portal. Its most accessible programmatic surface is its research output: the RMIT Research Repository runs on Clarivate's Esploro platform, and RMIT's research data is published via a Figshare-hosted repository whose records are exposed through the public Figshare REST API (api.figshare.com) and syndicated to Research Data Australia. Student-facing systems such as timetables, the curriculum catalogue, and identity/SSO sit behind authentication and are not offered as public APIs.

providers.name: University Startups
providers.description: University Startups is an AI-powered transition planning management platform built for special education teams. The platform helps teachers create IDEA-compliant IEP transition plans in under 10 minutes, audits plans against 11 IDEA Indicator 13 criteria in under 90 seconds, generates SMART-format IEP goals, and engages students with disabilities in building their own transition plans, alongside a college and career readiness curriculum and internship simulator. A Techstars portfolio company serving United States school districts including NYC Public Schools; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: Delightree
providers.description: Delightree is an AI-powered franchise operations platform that consolidates franchise management into a single operating system for headquarters and location teams. It combines a centralized knowledge base, interactive training, task management, forms and checklists, audits, a location launcher for opening new stores, team communication, and reporting so franchisors can standardize and enforce standard operating procedures across every location. The platform is built around frontline franchisee adoption and serves 150+ franchise brands across food and beverage, fitness, wellness, home services, and other multi-unit, regulated sectors. Backed by Accel; profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment (2026-07-18).

providers.name: Guidde
providers.description: Guidde is an AI-powered digital adoption and knowledge-capture platform that turns any on-screen workflow into professional step-by-step video documentation and how-to guides. Its Magic Capture browser extension, desktop, and mobile apps record a process, then AI generates a structured script, an AI voiceover (200+ voices), and an editable walkthrough that teams can translate into 50+ languages and embed wherever work happens. Guidde targets onboarding, customer education, support deflection, and internal process documentation for enterprises, and integrates with tools like Slack, Zendesk, Confluence, Notion, Salesforce, SharePoint, and ServiceNow. Guidde is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Guidde does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: BetterUp
providers.description: BetterUp is an enterprise Human Transformation Platform that combines human and AI-powered coaching, grounded in behavioral science and enterprise data, to help organizations develop leaders, managers, and their broader workforce. Founded by Alexi Robichaux, BetterUp serves 750+ enterprise customers including Google, Salesforce, Moderna, and Workday, with a network of 4,000+ coaches across 70+ countries. The platform delivers leadership development, manager effectiveness, AI coaching, and workforce resilience programs. BetterUp is HR-tech / organizational-development software and exposes no public developer API; platform integration is delivered through packaged enterprise connectors (Workday, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Viva, SAP SuccessFactors, Degreed) plus HRIS and SSO provisioning. Sector: hr-tech.

providers.name: Effectful
providers.description: Effectful Technologies is the company behind Effect, an open-source ecosystem of production-grade TypeScript libraries. The flagship `effect` library is a composable standard library and execution engine that unifies error handling, resource management, concurrency, dependency injection, observability, schema, and testability, letting developers focus on what a program should accomplish rather than how. Effect is positioned as "Layer 0" of a broader vision extending into distributed systems — RPC, SQL, clustering, AI integrations, and durable execution. The ecosystem ships as first-party npm packages under the `effect` and `@effect/*` scopes (MIT licensed) from the Effect-TS GitHub organization. Effectful is developer-tooling / library company, not an HTTP API provider, and is backed by Amplify Partners.

providers.name: Outset
providers.description: Outset is an AI-powered qualitative research platform, operated by Parnassus Labs, Inc., that lets enterprise research and product teams run large-scale AI-moderated interviews across video, voice, and text in 85+ countries and many languages. Its AI moderators conduct conversational interviews, an AI-driven synthesis layer produces summaries, themes, quotes, and highlight reels, and a Visual Intelligence suite analyzes visual cues during sessions. The platform includes participant recruitment against a large panel plus an AI fraud-detection agent. Customers include Microsoft, HubSpot, Nestle, Glassdoor, Coinbase, and Indeed. Outset publishes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 42001, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance posture but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tobii
providers.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

providers.name: Stepful
providers.description: Stepful is a New York-based healthcare workforce education company that trains people with a high-school education for entry-level allied-health roles in as little as four months. It runs live, cohort-based online programs — Medical Assistant, Pharmacy Technician, Patient Care Technician, Medical Administrative Assistant, Surgical Technologist, Dental Assistant, Phlebotomy Technician, Sterile Processing and Practical Nursing — pairing virtual instructor-led classes and 1:1 coaching with at-home clinical skills kits, employer-site clinical rotations and an AI-assisted practice platform, then places graduates into hospital and clinic jobs. Its "School-as-a-Service" employer product lets health systems stand up in-house training and upskilling pipelines. Stepful is backed by Y Combinator, Oak HC/FT and Reach Capital, has raised a $31.5M Series B and a $55M Series C, and reports having served more than 30,000 students. It is a Delaware corporation approved to operate by state career-school boards in Alabama, California, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas and Utah. Stepful publishes no public developer API: its student classroom and staff admin applications are both authenticated-only, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or webhook contract is served from any host it controls.

providers.name: University of Los Andes Colombia
providers.description: Universidad de los Andes (Uniandes) is a private research university in Bogota, Colombia, founded in 1948, and ranked #179 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its publicly observable developer/API footprint is limited: the strongest public machine-readable surface is the DSpace-based institutional repository "Seneca" (repositorio.uniandes.edu.co), which exposes an OAI-PMH metadata interface and a DSpace REST API for open-access scholarly content. Student-facing systems such as the Ellucian Banner SIS (MiBanner) are authentication-gated and do not publish public API documentation. No dedicated public developer portal or documented open API program was found at time of review.

providers.name: University of Navarra
providers.description: The University of Navarra (Universidad de Navarra) is a private research university founded in 1952, headquartered in Pamplona, Spain, with additional campuses in San Sebastian and Madrid. It is ranked #249 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-consumable developer footprint is limited: the principal documented interface is DADUN (Deposito Academico Digital de la Universidad de Navarra), the institutional open-access repository running on DSpace, which exposes metadata harvesting through the OAI-PMH protocol. No general-purpose public developer portal, open-data API platform, or official GitHub organization could be independently confirmed for the institution at the time of review.

providers.name: Khan Academy
providers.description: Khan Academy is a non-profit providing free online educational content. The legacy Khan Academy API (v1) is deprecated/limited and the public api-explorer.khanacademy.org redirects to the main site. Some endpoints under www.khanacademy.org/api/v1/ remain in use for internal apps and historical integrations, but Khan Academy no longer maintains a publicly supported developer program.

providers.name: Wonder Workshop
providers.description: Wonder Workshop (GitHub org "playi", originally Play-i) is an educational technology company that makes the Dash, Dot, and Cue programmable robots and the Make Wonder K-8 coding and robotics learning platform, used by more than 40,000 schools across 65 countries. Its developer surface is a set of official SDKs that give granular realtime control of the physical robots' sensors and actuators over Bluetooth Low Energy: WonderPy (Python, on PyPI), @wonderworkshop/wwjs (JavaScript, on npm), and an iOS/Android robot framework shipped in the playground sample-app repository. There is no HTTP/cloud REST API, OAuth, or webhook surface; integration happens locally over BLE. Backed by GV.

providers.name: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur
providers.description: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur / IIT KGP) is a public technical and research university in West Bengal, India, and the first of the IITs, ranked #222 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public digital footprint centers on machine-readable scholarly infrastructure rather than a formal developer program: the Central Library operates a DSpace-based Institutional Digital Repository (the first IR among the IITs) and the institute maintains an IRINS research-profile portal hosted by INFLIBNET that ingests data from ORCID, Scopus, and Crossref. Operational systems such as the ERP/SSO platform are gated to enrolled members and expose no public API documentation. No official institution-wide developer portal was found; this profile catalogs the publicly reachable, standards-based endpoints only.

providers.name: Speak
providers.description: Speak (Speakeasy Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered language learning application focused on spoken fluency rather than grammar drills or vocabulary memorization. Its proprietary "Speak Method" has learners study real phrases, practice them across contexts, and then apply them in back-and-forth conversation with an AI tutor that gives real-time pronunciation and fluency feedback. Speak teaches Spanish, French, Korean, Japanese, Italian, German, and Chinese, plus English for non-English speakers, and offers B2B language training for organizations across Korea, Japan, Spain, Taiwan, and France. The company is backed by Accel and the OpenAI Startup Fund and partners with OpenAI. Speak runs a production application backend at api.usespeak.com (an OAuth2/OIDC issuer) but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; the surfaces below were discovered from the company's public well-known and llms.txt endpoints.

providers.name: Illuminate Education
providers.description: Illuminate Education is a K-12 education technology company providing assessment, data analytics, and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) tools to schools and districts. Its platform serves roughly 17 million students across 5,200 schools and districts in all 50 states, taking a "whole child" approach that combines academic and social-emotional-behavioral data. Marquee products are FastBridge (universal screening and progress monitoring), DnA (standards-based assessment creation and scoring), and eduCLIMBER (MTSS collaboration and district data management). Illuminate does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI; data exchange runs through education-interoperability standards (LTI 1.0/1.1 Certified, OneRoster, Ed-Fi 2.5+, QTI) and partner/SIS/LMS integrations. It is a portfolio company of Insight Partners, headquartered in Irvine, California.

providers.name: Juno Journey
providers.description: Juno Journey is an AI-powered Learning & Development (L&D) platform that unifies employee training, personalized development planning, skills analytics, and performance management into a single "HumAIn Workforce Platform." Its Juno Agents automate course authoring, build adaptive personal development plans, deliver real-time in-context knowledge assistance, and surface live capability analytics, while a built-in LMS aggregates 150+ external content providers. The product connects to HRIS, identity, messaging, calendar, and performance systems through pre-built integrations (Slack, Okta, Workday, BambooHR, HiBob, Personio, Cornerstone, Google Drive, Microsoft Azure). Juno Journey is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site, pricing, a knowledge hub, a blog, a status page, and a public trust center (ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, CCPA) but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Playwright
providers.description: Playwright is an open-source framework from Microsoft for web automation and browser testing. It enables reliable end-to-end testing for modern web apps, supporting Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit browsers. Playwright is consumed as a library and CLI rather than a hosted HTTP API.

providers.name: Parse Biosciences
providers.description: Parse Biosciences is a Seattle-based life-sciences company that makes Evercode, a split-pool combinatorial barcoding chemistry for single cell and single nuclei RNA sequencing that runs on standard lab equipment rather than a dedicated microfluidics instrument. Its product line spans Evercode WT Mini, WT, WT Mega and WT Penta whole transcriptome kits, Evercode TCR and BCR immune profiling, Evercode Fixation, Evercode WT FFPE, Gene Select and CRISPR Detect, alongside a GigaLab sequencing service for 10M+ cell projects. Data analysis is delivered through Trailmaker, a cloud application that takes Evercode FASTQ files through a pipeline and into interactive downstream analysis. Parse publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; Trailmaker is an end-user web application whose backend is authenticated with AWS Cognito and undocumented outside the product.

providers.name: Aceable
providers.description: Aceable (Aceable Brands) is an Austin, Texas mobile-first online education company founded in 2013 that builds state-accredited licensing and continuing-education courses across four brands: Aceable (drivers ed, defensive driving and traffic school in 40+ US states), Aceable Agent (real estate pre-license, post-license and CE in 16 states, plus PrepAgent exam prep in all 50), Aceable Insurance (Property & Casualty and Life & Health pre-license in 13 states, CE in CA/IL/TX) and Aceable Mortgage (NMLS-approved MLO pre-license and CE in 7 states plus the required 20-hour national component; NMLS Provider ID 1400102). More than 20 million students have been licensed through Aceable, at roughly 1.5 million per year. The company raised about $106M across five rounds from Silverton Partners, Floodgate, Sageview Capital and HGGC, and operates a B2B partner program (affiliate and bulk-buy) for driving schools, school districts, brokerages, carriers and mortgage employers. Aceable publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its platform API at api.aceable.com is a private, application-ID-gated backend serving the Aceable web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Drillster
providers.description: Drillster is a digital learning platform that uses adaptive, repetition-based technology to help users acquire and retain knowledge and skills through personalized drills, quizzes, and learning modules.

providers.name: Real Estate Institute of Australia
providers.description: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA), founded in 1924 and based in Canberra, is the national federation of the eight state and territory Real Estate Institutes (REINSW, REIV, REIQ, REIWA, REISA, REIT, REIACT, REINT), which between them represent roughly 85% of Australian real estate businesses and agents. REIA is a policy, research and accreditation body, not an operator of market infrastructure: it administers the REIA National Principles of Conduct that underpin state institute codes and training, awards Associate (AREI) and Fellow accreditations, runs the Australasian Auctioneering Championships (AUSTROS) jointly with REINZ and the National Awards for Excellence (NAFE), makes submissions to the Commonwealth Government, and publishes the quarterly Housing Affordability Report (HAR) and Real Estate Market Facts (REMF) series that Federal Treasury, the Reserve Bank, state treasuries and investment banks subscribe to. It sits well above the transaction rail in the Australian value chain - listings run through REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain, settlement through PEXA, valuation through PropTrack and CoreLogic, and title through the state land registries - and REIA touches none of those pipes. Its API posture is therefore an honest absence: no developer portal, no API subdomain, no OpenAPI or OData contract, and no RESO reference anywhere on its estate, because RESO is a NAR-mandated United States construct with no Australian counterpart. What REIA sells is data, not access to it - the HAR and REMF reports are AUD 450 subscriptions and each of the 7 HAR and 15 REMF underlying datasets is a separate AUD 280 subscription, delivered as documents through a platformOS/Insites ecommerce storefront with Stripe checkout behind an email-and-password account. Policy submissions, standalone research reports and the strategic plan are freely downloadable PDFs; the quarterly numbers are not, and there is no open data.

providers.name: Cuemath
providers.description: Cuemath is an India-headquartered education technology company founded in 2013 by Manan Khurma that delivers live, one-to-one online math tutoring to students in grades K through 12 across more than 80 countries. Its MathFit framework and LEAP learning platform pair certified tutors with an interactive, gamified curriculum aligned to US Common Core standards, spanning arithmetic, algebra, geometry, pre-calculus, AP calculus and standardized test preparation. Cuemath sells directly to families as a subscription tutoring product; it operates a consumer web and mobile application rather than a developer platform, and publishes no public API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: EvolveApp INC.
providers.description: EvolveApp INC. (Evolve) is an AI-native enablement and performance platform for corporate learning and workforce training. Its product suite spans the Evolve LMS for courses, learning paths and branded academies; Evolve Generate for AI-powered course creation from raw materials; Evolve Studio for advanced authoring; an Assessment Center for skills and behavioral evaluation; an AI Knowledge Base instant-answer engine; and AI-driven Simulations for job-critical practice. Evolve serves 100+ enterprise clients and 2.9M+ learners worldwide, is SOC 2 (Type 1 and 2), ISO 27001 and GDPR compliant, and offers iOS and Android apps. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Unmind
providers.description: Unmind is a workplace mental health platform that supports employees, develops leaders, and strengthens organisational performance through therapy, coaching, manager training, crisis care, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), wellbeing content, insights and assessments, and Nova, an AI wellbeing coach. Customers include Uber, MLB, Samsung, British Airways, Diageo, and the NHS. Unmind publishes no public developer API; api.unmind.com is a private Apollo GraphQL backend serving its own apps.

providers.name: IgGenix
providers.description: IgGenix, Inc. is a clinical-stage antibody discovery and development company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 on work from Stephen Quake's laboratory at Stanford in collaboration with allergy clinician-researcher Kari Nadeau. Its SEQ SIFTER platform uses single-cell RNA sequencing to capture the rare IgE-producing B cells circulating in allergic patients' blood, then re-engineers those sequences into fully human, high-affinity, allergen-specific IgG antibodies designed to block the allergic cascade before it starts. Lead program IGNX001 is a human IgG4 monoclonal antibody for peanut allergy, in the Phase 1 ACCELERATE Peanut trial, with discovery programs against alpha-gal syndrome, nsLTP allergens and atopic dermatitis autoantigens. The company has raised roughly $75M across seed, Series A and a $40M Series B. IgGenix publishes no product or developer API and no developer program; the only machine-readable surface on iggenix.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) served at https://iggenix.com/wp-json/, which returns the company's press releases, peer-reviewed publications, conference abstracts, careers post type, pages, media library, taxonomies and site search as anonymous JSON. The OpenAPI definitions in this repository were derived mechanically from that route index; IgGenix publishes none of its own.

providers.name: MentorCloud
providers.description: MentorCloud is an AI-enabled, enterprise mentoring software platform that helps organizations optimize employee engagement, retention, and career development through structured mentoring programs. It serves HR and Learning & Development teams and enterprise leaders looking to scale human-led learning across engineering, management, higher education, hospitality, and non-profit contexts. The platform covers mentor/mentee matching, program management, sessions, circles, learning, and community, with use cases spanning new-hire onboarding, leadership development, career progression, and Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) initiatives. MentorCloud is delivered as a hosted B2B SaaS product with managed, custom two-way integrations to enterprise CRM, HR, and single sign-on systems rather than a self-serve public developer API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Civitas Learning
providers.description: Civitas Learning is a higher education technology company whose Student Impact Platform unifies student data, predictive analytics, and coordinated workflows to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, persistence, and completion outcomes. The platform consolidates data from SIS, LMS, CRM, and event systems into a data lakehouse, layers institution-specific predictive models (CivIQ) on top, and surfaces real-time, actionable insights to advisors, faculty, and administrators through products such as Explore, Inspire, Impact, Illume, College Scheduler, Degree Map, and Academic Planning. Civitas Learning serves institutions of all sizes and pairs its software with strategic advisory services. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public operational, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: 3P Learning Pty
providers.description: 3P Learning is an educational technology company that builds blended learning software for mathematics and literacy used by schools and families worldwide. Its product family includes Mathletics, Mathseeds, Reading Eggs, Writing Legends, LiteracyPlanet and Brightpath, reaching more than 20 million students across 130+ countries. The programs pair interactive student activities with teacher dashboards, reporting and curriculum-aligned content, and integrate into school systems via single sign-on and rostering standards such as Clever and LTI. 3P Learning is backed by Insight Partners and profiled in the API Evangelist network. This company publishes consumer and school-facing web and mobile products but does not expose a public first-party developer API or documented API surface.

providers.name: creativeLIVE
providers.description: creativeLIVE (CreativeLive) is an online learning platform offering more than 2,300 on-demand courses and live interactive classes taught by working professionals across photography, video and filmmaking, graphic and web design, business and entrepreneurship, arts and crafts, audio and music production, and AI and technology. Learners access practical, skill-based instruction through a subscription, with certificates of completion available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; creativeLIVE exposes no public developer API, but does publish a machine-readable llms.txt course index for AI agents.

providers.name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
providers.description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem (HUJI) is Israel's leading research university, ranked #272 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates multiple campuses in Jerusalem, Rehovot, and Eilat across the humanities, sciences, medicine, and law. HUJI does not publish a dedicated public developer portal or documented open API program. Its developer-relevant surface is limited to standards-based academic infrastructure: an Ex Libris Primo/Alma library discovery system (whose APIs require institution-issued keys), the OpenScholar profile/CMS platform, Shibboleth/SAML single sign-on (internal/gated), and a number of research-lab open-source GitHub organizations. No public, self-service API endpoints were confirmed.

providers.name: Indian Institute of Technology Madras
providers.description: Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) is a public technical and research university in Chennai, India, ranked #227 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates an institutional website (iitm.ac.in), a central library with electronic databases, a large online BS degree program in Data Science and Applications, and SSO/OAuth2-based identity endpoints. As of this review IIT Madras does not publish a public, documented developer portal or open API program. Its official GitHub organization exists but currently exposes no public repositories. The properties cataloged below reflect only publicly confirmed institutional web properties and identity endpoints, not documented third-party APIs.

providers.name: KiwiCo
providers.description: KiwiCo, Inc. is a direct-to-consumer education company headquartered in Mountain View, California, founded in 2011 by Sandra Oh Lin. KiwiCo designs and ships hands-on STEAM (science, technology, engineering, art and math) project kits — branded as crates — on a monthly subscription, with distinct lines aimed at every age from infants through teens and adults, alongside single-purchase kits sold through its online store. A KiwiCo Education division supplies the same project kits and NGSS-aligned lesson guides to schools, homeschools, after-school programs and camps. KiwiCo operates as a consumer e-commerce and subscription business and publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, CLI or webhook surface, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents on any of its hosts. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Queen Mary University of London
providers.description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is a public research university in London, United Kingdom, and a member of the Russell Group, ranked #120 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-oriented rather than a formal developer program: Queen Mary Research Online (QMRO) is an open-access DSpace institutional repository that exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, and the university maintains a public GitHub organization (QMUL) for code released by its staff. QMUL does not publish a central, branded developer portal with signup-gated REST APIs; core student, timetable, and library platforms (QMplus/Moodle, MyQMUL, library discovery) sit behind institutional authentication.

providers.name: Queensland University of Technology
providers.description: Queensland University of Technology (QUT) is a public research university based in Brisbane, Australia, ranked #213 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. QUT serves around 50,000 students with an applied emphasis in teaching and research. Its public, machine-accessible developer footprint is modest and centered on open research infrastructure: the QUT ePrints institutional repository exposes a live OAI-PMH metadata harvesting interface, and QUT maintains several active research-group GitHub organizations (eResearch, Centre for Robotics, Aerospace Systems, Digital Observatory). Most other institutional systems (Library Search built on Ex Libris Primo VE / Alma, the Timetable Planner, the QUT mobile app backend, and the SSO identity layer) are internal or gated and do not publish open developer documentation.

providers.name: Tianjin University
providers.description: Tianjin University (TJU) is a national public research university in Tianjin, China, founded in 1895 as Peiyang University and recognized as the oldest modern university in China. It is ranked #269 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. TJU operates the usual institutional web properties (official site, library OPAC, faculty and international-cooperation portals) but does not publish a public developer portal or documented, openly accessible API. No public API documentation, base URLs, or sign-up flows could be verified at the time of cataloging; the entries below reflect only confirmed public web properties, not documented APIs.

providers.name: Tynker
providers.description: Tynker is a coding platform for kids and teens ages 5-18 that makes it fun to learn programming through game-based, interactive courses, with students starting in visual block-based coding and progressing to real-world languages like Python and JavaScript. The platform powers the creativity of over 100 million students and serves thousands of schools and educators worldwide, spanning home plans for parents, K-12 school curriculum, Hour of Code activities, and Minecraft modding. Tynker is a 500 Global and Felicis portfolio company, now part of CodeHS, and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Wuhan University
providers.description: Wuhan University (WHU), founded in 1893 and located in Wuhan, Hubei, China, is one of China's oldest and most prestigious comprehensive research universities, ranked #194 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates under the Ministry of Education of China and is recognized for surveying and remote sensing, geoinformatics, and the sciences. WHU does not publish a centralized, publicly documented developer or API portal; its official web presence (en.whu.edu.cn) is informational only. Discoverable developer activity is concentrated in research-group GitHub organizations rather than institutional API products. No public, documented institutional API endpoints could be confirmed at the time of review.

providers.name: Multiverse
providers.description: Multiverse is a British education-technology company (founded 2016 by Euan Blair and Sophie Adelman, headquartered in London) that operates an AI-adoption and workforce-upskilling platform. It delivers apprenticeships and training programmes in AI, data, software engineering, and digital skills, pairing on-the-job learning with expert coaching so employers can close skills gaps and build future-ready teams. Backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, General Catalyst, and StepStone Group, Multiverse serves enterprise clients across the UK and US. The company exposes no public developer API; its digital surface is a marketing site, a learner/employer login, a help centre, a community hub, a blog, a service status page, and a trust centre.

providers.name: UpCodes
providers.description: UpCodes is a comprehensive compliance and product research platform for the construction industry, offering a searchable database of US construction and building codes consolidated by state and city for easier navigation. The platform includes libraries of codes, diagrams, and assemblies, project collaboration and bookmarking, code calculators with a BIM design data import tool, SAML single sign-on for enterprise teams, and an AI Copilot that answers code compliance questions, locates assemblies, and generates project-specific checklists. Plans span Essentials, Professional, and Enterprise tiers. UpCodes does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Wonderschool
providers.description: Wonderschool is a child care platform that connects families with licensed care and equips providers with software and services to start, operate, and grow their child care programs. It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

providers.name: beva
providers.description: beva (贝瓦网), operated by ProKids Technology Corp / 芝兰玉树（北京）科技股份有限公司, is a Chinese IP-and-technology driven family education and entertainment company. Its flagship original IP is the little beaver "Beva" (贝瓦) and the "Beva Children's Songs" (贝瓦儿歌) brand, spanning children's music, animation, literature and interactive entertainment, distributed across web, mobile, OTT, IPTV and television channels. Through its ProKids Copyright Content Open Platform (open.beva.com) beva offers online-application and offline content-access APIs that let third-party mobile apps and smart hardware — story machines, smart speakers and kids' robots such as MiTu, Rokid and the Doraemon story machine — embed licensed children's audio and video content. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Coachup
providers.description: CoachUp is the nation's leading private sports coaching marketplace, founded in 2012 in Boston by Jordan Fliegel, Arian Radmand, and Gabe Durazo. It connects athletes of all levels — and the parents of young athletes — with vetted, background-checked private and small-group coaches across basketball, soccer, football, baseball, running and track and field, volleyball, swimming, softball, tennis, lacrosse, fitness, and dance. Coaches are discoverable by sport and location, sessions average $40–$60 per hour, and every session is backed by $1 million liability insurance. The platform has hosted more than 13,000 coaches serving over 100,000 athletes, with Boston, New York, Los Angeles, Dallas, and Chicago among its top training markets. CoachUp is backed by General Catalyst, Point Judith Capital, and Techstars. As of this profile CoachUp exposes only a consumer web and mobile experience with no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Headspace
providers.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.

providers.name: Ulysses (Kaminashi)
providers.description: Kaminashi Inc. (株式会社カミナシ) is a Tokyo-based SaaS company founded in December 2016 under its former corporate name Ulysses Inc. (ユリシーズ株式会社). It builds the Kaminashi frontline-operations DX platform for deskless workers — digital checklists and inspections, equipment maintenance (CMMS), frontline employee management, training and manuals, and reporting — serving food manufacturing, machine manufacturing, logistics, hotels, and building maintenance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and a16z. The company is ISMS (ISO/IEC 27001) certified and publishes no public developer API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Blomma
providers.description: Blomma is an AI-powered career coaching platform that pairs artificial intelligence with emotional intelligence to act as a private thinking partner for professionals. Through chat-based coaching, guided reflection, goal-setting with built-in accountability, a personal journal, and a growth dashboard, Blomma helps founders, people leaders, and ambitious professionals turn abstract aspirations into concrete, trackable goals, and can personalize coaching from uploaded performance reviews and development plans. It is delivered as a consumer subscription through web and mobile apps, with custom team plans for organizations, and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Lateral
providers.description: Lateral was a Berlin- and Hobart-based AI research software company founded in 2013 that built machine-learning powered content recommendation and document navigation tools. Its early product was a conceptual text-matching and recommendation API that let developers insert documents and retrieve semantically similar content, with pre-populated corpora covering arXiv, PubMed, Wikipedia, news and SEC filings. The company later pivoted to an LLM-assisted research workspace for navigating information across large document sets, and published open-source research on hyperbolic-space word embeddings (Poincare embeddings, hyperplane hashers, WARP recommenders). Lateral was permanently shut down on 26 June 2025; the team pointed users to a successor open-source research platform at coordination.network. The public API, its documentation host and the application host are all retired, so this profile documents a historical API surface and the client libraries that remain published.

providers.name: MIT
providers.description: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) operates an internal developer portal that exposes APIs for the institution's information systems. The MIT developer environment publishes APIs such as the Roles API for managing institutional roles and authorizations. Access to the developer portal and most APIs requires MIT authentication via Shibboleth / Touchstone single sign-on, making the catalog primarily available to community members, partners, and authorized integrators rather than to the general public.

providers.name: Aristotle
providers.description: Aristotle (heyaristotle.com) is an AI tutoring platform that delivers personalized, one-on-one, dialogue-based instruction across all subjects. Rather than lecturing or simply marking answers wrong, it uses a Socratic, voice-first approach to diagnose conceptual misconceptions and verifies each response turn-by-turn before delivering it to the student. Positioned as an affordable alternative to human tutors, its methodology is grounded in learning science (Bloom's two-sigma work, ICAP, LearnLM benchmarks). Backed by True Ventures. Sector: EdTech / AI education. No public developer API or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Caliber Fitness
providers.description: Caliber Fitness, Inc. is a consumer strength-training and fitness-coaching company behind the Caliber: Strength Training app (iOS and Android). Caliber combines data-driven resistance-training and nutrition programming, a library of 600+ exercises, workout tracking, and one-on-one video coaching from certified personal trainers across free, Caliber Plus, and Premium Coaching tiers. Founded by Justin Fauci and Chris Muir, the company is backed by Trinity Ventures. Caliber operates as a consumer mobile app and coaching service; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. This profile tracks its public web, legal, and membership surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Campus
providers.description: Campus (campus.edu) is an accredited, for-profit online community college offering associate degree programs built on the CUNY ASAP high-touch support model, with live classes taught by faculty from top universities, personal success coaching, and tuition capped at the Pell Grant maximum. Founded by Tade Oyerinde and backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Bloomberg Beta, 8VC, Rethink Education and others, Campus focuses on affordable, accessible higher education and career preparation across programs such as applied AI, business, information technology and healthcare administration. This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public web surface; Campus is a consumer education provider and publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Simpleclub
providers.description: Simpleclub is a German digital learning platform serving over two million students (grades 5-13), apprentices, and organizations across school, vocational training (Ausbildung), continuing education, retraining, and workforce upskilling.
