The product pairs curriculum-aligned content (including IHK-aligned vocational tracks) with an AI-powered learning assistant, trainer/learning-management tooling, and the ability for organizations to upload custom content. It counts 750+ corporate clients such as Deutsche Bahn, Bosch, and Vodafone. Simpleclub maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source Flutter tooling (math keyboard, flutter_math, design-token builder) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification; this profile is an end-user/EdTech company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Atom Learning
providers.description: Atom Learning is a UK edtech company providing an online, adaptive exam-preparation and learning platform for children aged 7 to 16. Its consumer product, Atom Home, delivers personalised practice, unlimited mock tests with instant marking, and progress tracking for 11+ grammar and independent-school entrance exams (GL, CEM, CSSE, ISEB), CAT4, Key Stage 2 SATs, and GCSE revision. Its schools product, Atom School, gives teachers curriculum-mapped resources and assessment tools and is used by over 1,000 schools. Founded by educators and assessment specialists, Atom has supported hundreds of thousands of families as a lower-cost alternative to private tutoring. The company was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer web/app product surface but no public developer API.

providers.name: Capella University
providers.description: Capella University is an accredited online university owned by Strategic Education, Inc. (SEI), offering competency-based bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees plus graduate certificates across business, counseling and therapy, education, health sciences, information technology, nursing, psychology, and social work. Capella is regionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and delivers coursework through two learning formats — FlexPath, a self-paced competency-based model, and GuidedPath, a structured-timeline model — serving working adults and professional learners entirely online.

providers.name: Complori
providers.description: Complori is a Berlin, Germany based online education company that teaches children and young people to code through live, small-group video classes led by qualified coaches in a protected digital space. Its programs span programming with Minecraft, Python, JavaScript game development, app development, and financial literacy, backed by a learning platform with challenges and exercises, a mobile learning app, completion certificates, flexible family-friendly scheduling, and holiday camps. Complori operates a B2C consumer education service (with parents as the decision-makers) rather than a developer-facing API product, and runs an education scholarship program to broaden access across socioeconomic backgrounds. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: DIY
providers.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Home From College
providers.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Interintellect
providers.description: Interintellect is the world's leading salon platform, a creator-led cultural center for intellectual conversation founded in March 2019 by art philosopher Anna Gat. The platform lets people attend and host high-quality salons and discussions online and offline, across philosophy, technology, poetry, history, and the arts, building community around shared intellectual interests. It supports independent thinkers and hosts through ticket revenue, training, and a peer community, with paid membership tiers granting event access, members-only sessions, community forums, and global in-person gatherings. Interintellect is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; it publishes no public API or developer platform, so this profile carries identity and website-property signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Smore
providers.description: Smore is a newsletter and flyer builder purpose-built for educators, schools, and districts, letting teachers and administrators create accessible, mobile-friendly digital newsletters from customizable templates to keep families and staff informed. The product emphasizes WCAG AA accessibility, translation for multilingual families, and engagement analytics on opens and clicks. Smore is now part of SchoolStatus, the family-engagement platform. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Smore publishes no public developer program, API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface — this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture only.

providers.name: CaaMTech
providers.description: CaaMTech is a pharmaceutical drug discovery company in Issaquah, Washington, founded by Dr. Andrew Chadeayne, engineering next-generation psychedelic-inspired small-molecule therapeutics for mental health conditions. It synthesizes and characterizes novel tryptamines, screens natural and synthetic compounds for safety and efficacy, publishes fundamental crystallographic and pharmacological research, and builds a patent portfolio around the results. CaaMTech operates no developer program and publishes no product API; the only machine-readable surface on caam.tech is the standard WordPress REST API that serves the company site, which does make its research updates, pages and media programmatically readable without credentials, alongside an authenticated WordPress MCP adapter endpoint.

providers.name: NutriSense
providers.description: NutriSense is a metabolic health and wellness company that pairs continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with 1:1 registered-dietitian coaching and a mobile app. Members receive glucose biosensors, real-time and historical glucose analytics, AI-assisted pattern insights, stress-management sessions, and video consults with credentialed, glucose-certified nutritionists to build sustainable nutrition, weight-loss, and metabolic-health habits. Nutrisense runs a consumer product with a member web and mobile app experience; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It does publish a machine-readable llms.txt at nutrisense.io/llms.txt.

providers.name: Branchtrack
providers.description: BranchTrack is a browser-based authoring platform for building interactive branching scenarios and conversation simulations used in corporate learning and development. Instructional designers and L&D teams create decision-tree simulations with no coding or design skills, then deploy them inside existing LMS platforms or embed them into courses authored in Articulate Storyline, Rise, Adobe Captivate, Gomo, and Lectora. Simulations export as SCORM and xAPI (Tin Can) packages and can be shared as responsive, mobile-native experiences with learner analytics and completion tracking. BranchTrack is a portfolio company of Seedcamp. The platform exposes no first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; third-party embedding is available via the Embedly oEmbed provider, and LMS delivery via SCORM/xAPI.

providers.name: GoPillar
providers.description: GoPillar (operated by CoContest Italy Srl, Rome, Italy) is a crowdsourced architectural and interior design marketplace where homeowners, businesses, and small construction firms launch online design contests and receive dozens of proposals from a global community of 70,000+ registered architects and designers. Clients set a project timeline, brief the community, message participating designers, and select the winning concept, with follow-on one-to-one and offline executive-project services. GoPillar also runs GoPillar Academy, an e-learning platform offering professional BIM, 3D, and design courses plus custom corporate training for architecture and construction firms. GoPillar is a consumer/SMB web platform and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lalilo
providers.description: Lalilo is an adaptive reading and literacy web application for primary-school classrooms, founded in Paris in 2016 and acquired by Renaissance (Wisconsin Rapids, USA) in 2021. It delivers roughly 90,000 interactive phonics, fluency and comprehension exercises that adapt in real time to each student, uses speech recognition to assess oral reading aloud, and gives teachers a dashboard for tracking progress and running differentiated small-group instruction. It is used by around 40,000 teachers and 400,000 students a year in France across cycles 2 and 3, with explicit support for DYS, allophone, ULIS, SEGPA and IME learners. Lalilo publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation: the product is consumed through the teacher and student web applications at app.lalilo.com, and integration or rostering questions are handled through Renaissance support rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: IKI AI
providers.description: IKI AI is an AI-native workspace for knowledge, research, strategy, and creative work, backed by 500 Global. It pairs an AI assistant that summarizes, highlights, and connects saved content with an AI editor that grounds writing in a user's personal knowledge base, plus shared Team Spaces and a browser extension for one-click webpage saving with notes. The product targets researchers, students, consultants, copywriters, coaches, lawyers, founders, and venture teams, and emphasizes privacy with a choice of top-tier LLMs. IKI AI is delivered as a consumer and team SaaS (web app at app.iki.ai and a Chrome extension) with subscription plans; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. This profile tracks its public identity, commercial, and security surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chemius
providers.description: Chemius is a cloud-based chemical compliance platform that automates Safety Data Sheet (SDS), Technical Data Sheet (TDS), and regulatory label creation in 38+ languages for organizations handling chemical products. The platform exposes an API suite covering SDS, TDS, ADR transport documentation, ERP integration, labels, web shop product data, and PDF generation, and offers AI-assisted authoring through the Chemius AI SDS assistant. Chemius is hosted in DIN ISO/IEC 27001-certified German data centers and supports CLP 1272/2008, REACH 1907/2006, detergents, aerosols, and US OSHA / GHS regulatory frameworks.

providers.name: Duolingo
providers.description: Duolingo (NASDAQ: DUOL) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based learning technology company best known for the Duolingo language-learning app, the world's most-downloaded education app, offering courses in more than 40 languages including Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and Chinese. Founded in 2011 by Luis von Ahn and Severin Hacker, Duolingo has expanded its consumer learning footprint beyond languages with Duolingo Math, Duolingo Music, a newly rolled-out Chess course, and Duolingo ABC for early literacy, all delivered through the same gamified, streak- driven mobile experience. The Company also operates the Duolingo English Test, a digital English-proficiency exam accepted by thousands of higher- education institutions, certification programs, and government agencies worldwide as an alternative to TOEFL and IELTS. Duolingo monetizes through Super Duolingo and Duolingo Max subscriptions, in-app advertising, in-app purchases, and Duolingo English Test fees. The company surpassed 50 million daily active users in Q3 2025 and reported 41% revenue growth in Q2 2025. Duolingo does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with the Duolingo English Test (score-send to institutional CRMs such as Slate) are handled through a private API-key program negotiated directly with accepting institutions. Community- maintained reverse-engineered clients exist against the unofficial https://www.duolingo.com/api/1 surface but are not endorsed by Duolingo.

providers.name: Inkling
providers.description: Inkling is a frontline employee training and enablement platform (now part of Echo360) that delivers mission-critical knowledge, learning pathways, and operational workflows to essential workers across retail, hospitality, healthcare, and manufacturing. Its products include the Habitat content authoring tool, mobile Knowledge & Training modules, InkForms operational checklists, certification pathways, reporting and analytics, and LMS/LXP integrations. Inkling publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through LMS/LXP connectors and professional services. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched with the provider's public identity, security posture, and site properties.

providers.name: Ruzuku
providers.description: Ruzuku is a hosted online course platform for coaches, authors, and subject matter experts to create, teach, and sell online courses and learning communities. Ruzuku does not publish a documented public REST API or developer program. Its programmatic surface is exposed exclusively through a Zapier integration - authenticated with an API Key, API Secret, and Site URL generated under Account then Integrations then Configure Zapier - that offers event triggers (enrollments, lesson and course completions, quiz and assignment submissions, comments, cancellations) and a small set of student enroll, unenroll, and lookup actions. The APIs modeled below are honest logical groupings of that Zapier-mediated surface, not endpoints from a public Ruzuku API reference.

providers.name: Showbie
providers.description: Showbie is a K-12 learning platform for iPad that streamlines teaching workflows across assignments, feedback, grading, and classroom communication for teachers, students, and parents. Backed by Point Nine, it combines a digital classroom, annotation and file-sharing tools, and messaging into a single app used by schools worldwide. Showbie exposes no public developer API, SDK, or docs surface; this profile captures the company's public web, support, compliance, privacy, and terms properties, plus a live domain security probe.

providers.name: Economic Research Service
providers.description: The Economic Research Service (ERS) is a division of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) that conducts economic research and analysis related to agriculture, food, and rural development. ERS provides policymakers, stakeholders, and the public with valuable information and data to help inform decision-making and policy development.

providers.name: Fiveable
providers.description: Fiveable is an Advanced Placement (AP) exam preparation platform covering all 38 AP subjects. It provides study guides, unit-organized subject review hubs, practice questions modeled on real AP exam formats, AI-scored free-response questions (FRQs), cheatsheets, key-term glossaries, and AP score calculators that predict likely exam outcomes. Fiveable serves three audiences - secondary students cramming and reviewing for AP exams, teachers seeking classroom and assessment materials, and schools needing district-wide exam-prep support. The platform blends traditional study resources with AI-powered scoring and feedback. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Fiveable publishes a consumer web application but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Gronda
providers.description: Gronda is a professional community and learning platform for chefs and hospitality professionals, offering 70+ masterclasses and 20,000+ exclusive restaurant recipes from leading chefs, a chef directory and creator program, and team and culinary-school plans. Members share culinary creations, follow world-class chefs, and access PRO subscription content through the Gronda web and mobile apps. Backed by Speedinvest, Gronda was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; it is a consumer/community product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: jQuery
providers.description: jQuery is a fast, small, and feature-rich JavaScript library that makes HTML document traversal and manipulation, event handling, animation, and Ajax much simpler with an easy-to-use API that works across a multitude of browsers. Only about 30kB minified and gzipped, available as an AMD module, and CSS3 compliant. jQuery 4.0 is the current release; jQuery 3.x receives critical updates only.

providers.name: WizerMe
providers.description: WizerMe (Wizer) is an edtech platform used by more than 700,000 teachers to build interactive, self-grading digital worksheets. Educators turn existing PDFs and documents into engaging assessments with multiple-choice, video, audio, open-response, and puzzle question types, record video or audio instructions, apply differentiation rules, monitor student work in real time, schedule availability and time limits, and sync grades with Google Classroom. Students submit answers as text, audio, or video. Wizer offers a free tier (Wizer Create) and a premium tier (Wizer Boost) plus school and district plans, and is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Brisk Teaching
providers.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.

providers.name: Gnowbe
providers.description: Gnowbe is an AI-powered workforce enablement and performance platform for enterprise learning, enablement, and alignment. It turns static content and communication into mobile-first microlearning experiences with AI-powered activation and execution tracking, so teams do not just learn but perform. Trusted by 500,000+ learners across 100+ countries, Gnowbe combines authoring, AI content creation, group-based delivery, completion and engagement analytics, and integrations (SSO/SAML, LMS/SCORM, xAPI/LRS, HR systems, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Zapier's 5,000+ tools). Gnowbe is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Brainly
providers.description: Brainly is an education technology company founded in 2009 in Krakow, Poland (originally Zadane.pl) and now headquartered in New York City. It operates the world's largest online learning and homework-help community, a gamified, crowdsourced social-learning network where students, parents, and teachers ask and answer academic questions with verified answers from peers, educators, and Brainly's proprietary AI. As of 2025 the platform serves over 350 million monthly users across roughly 35 countries and has evolved from a community Q&A product into an agentic AI Learning Companion spanning homework help, AI tutoring, test prep, and classroom participation. Brainly is a consumer subscription business (Brainly Plus); it publishes no official public developer API — this profile captures its public web, security, and policy surface.

providers.name: Bridgetown Research
providers.description: Bridgetown Research is an AI-powered research and analysis platform that helps organizations analyze businesses with speed and precision. Its AI agents conduct expert interviews, gather primary and secondary data at scale, and execute 300+ of the most common analyses to power autonomous market research and commercial due diligence. The platform serves private equity and venture capital firms, professional services firms, and corporate strategy and development teams, who access it either through a SOC 2-compliant SaaS platform with interactive generative-search reporting or via an email-driven workflow that returns PDF reports. Bridgetown Research also exposes a REST API (documented on Apidog at docs.bridgetownresearch.com) for creating research projects and managing experts, expert actions, and scheduled calls. It is backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: CircuitLab
providers.description: CircuitLab, Inc. is an in-browser schematic capture and circuit simulation platform that lets engineers, students, educators, and hobbyists design and analyze analog and digital electronics systems before building a physical prototype. Running entirely in the browser with no installation, it offers schematic capture, mixed-signal SPICE-style simulation (DC, AC, transient, frequency-domain), custom device models and symbols, expression-based parameters, and shareable, exportable documentation. CircuitLab also publishes an electronics curriculum (CircuitLab Academy, the Ultimate Electronics textbook), community forums, and an electronics Q&A. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Y Combinator. At the time of this enrichment pass CircuitLab publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API description, so this profile captures its public web identity only.

providers.name: Wited (Portal Educativo)
providers.description: Wited (formerly Portal Educativo) is a Chilean edtech company backed by 500 Global that delivers online academic support and homeschooling across Latin America. Its two products - Reforzamiento (tutoring, homework help, and exam prep for K-12 students in traditional schools) and Colegio Online (a complete online school for homeschoolers) - combine curriculum-aligned courses, interactive exercises, the Max AI tutoring chatbot, live teacher support (Profes Express), and a parent progress dashboard. Wited operates in Chile, Mexico, Colombia, Panama, Argentina, Brazil, Spain, and the United States. The consumer platform runs at app.wited.com against a private backend (api.wited.com); the company publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Gartner
providers.description: Gartner is a global research and advisory firm providing information, advice, and tools to business leaders across IT, finance, HR, customer service, sales, marketing, supply chain, and legal functions. Gartner does not publish a public developer API; this repository tracks the company and any partner or technical artifacts that surface over time.

providers.name: The Block
providers.description: The Block is a New York-based digital-assets research, analysis, and news brand founded in 2018, covering cryptocurrency, blockchain, and Web3 markets. Its subscription platform, The Block Pro, packages breaking news, in-depth research, proprietary datasets, and venture-funding intelligence for professional investors, funds, and enterprises. The Block Pro also exposes a set of license-gated APIs - a real-time News API (REST, request-only, JSON), a Deals/Funding API, an Ecosystems/Data API, and a WebSocket news stream - available only to organizations holding a Block Pro subscription. The APIs have no public developer portal or OpenAPI definition; access and technical documentation are arranged through The Block's client-services team.

providers.name: Edyoucated
providers.description: Edyoucated is a German SaaS company offering an AI-powered corporate learning and skills-management platform for mid-to-large enterprises. The product combines a learning management / learning experience system (central management of training, mandatory compliance training, seminar administration, AI-assisted content creation, blended learning, and learning analytics) with skills management (skill cataloging, assessments, gap analysis, expert identification, and career guidance) to give organizations a common language for skills and personalized learning pathways. It also offers consulting for custom skill-taxonomy development. Customers include Deutsche Bahn, BASF, Shopware, and Finanz Informatik. Edyoucated is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer/API surface, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation.

providers.name: IXL Learning
providers.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

providers.name: ApplyBoard
providers.description: ApplyBoard is a study-abroad application platform that simplifies the international education journey by connecting students, recruitment partners, and partner schools on a single platform. Students explore and apply to more than 1,500 global universities and colleges across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and Germany, with supporting services spanning financial products, English-language test vouchers, and accommodation. ApplyBoard also operates ApplyProof, a document-verification and trust product. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK; its programmatic surface (including ApplyProof) is partner-gated. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prenda
providers.description: Prenda, Inc. is a Mesa, Arizona education technology company that makes it possible for an adult to open and run a K-8 microschool — a tight-knit learning community of roughly five to ten students — out of a home, studio, or office. Founded by Kelly Smith out of the Prenda Code Club he started at a public library in 2013, Prenda opened its first microschool in January 2018 and now supports more than 1,000 "guides" running microschools for nearly 10,000 learners across multiple US states, funded largely through school-choice and education savings account programs. The product is a plug-and-play software platform bundled with curriculum, training, and coaching: guides use it to manage enrollment, run adaptive diagnostic assessments in math and reading, track learner progress against Prenda's four-mode "connect, conquer, collaborate, create" learning day, process payments, and publish a marketing site for their school. Prenda is venture-backed, having raised a $20M round led by 776 in 2022. The platform is closed and end-user facing — Prenda publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only public developer surface is the Prenda Design System, an open-source MUI v6 React component and icon library published from the prenda-school GitHub organization.

providers.name: Rilla
providers.description: Rilla is an AI conversation-intelligence and coaching platform built for in-person and outside sales teams. Reps record their face-to-face customer conversations, and Rilla transcribes and analyzes them so managers can run virtual "ridealongs" and deliver targeted, data-driven coaching at scale. The platform surfaces talk patterns, objection handling, and outcome analytics across thousands of field conversations to help teams raise close rates, increase ticket size, and speed up rep ramp. Rilla is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the AI sector. Rilla runs a real production API — api.rillavoice.com/api/v1/, the private backend of its web and mobile apps, which answers every path with 401 Invalid Token — plus an AWS API Gateway webhook receiver its partner SPOTIO documents, but it publishes no developer portal, reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its CRM integrations are delivered by consuming the Merge unified API rather than by exposing a contract. This record captures its public web identity, the RFC 9116 security.txt it serves from app.rilla.com, and live domain-security and well-known probes.

providers.name: 80,000 Hours
providers.description: 80,000 Hours is an independent nonprofit, founded in 2011 by Benjamin Todd and William MacAskill out of Oxford, that provides free research and support to help people use their careers to help solve the world's most pressing problems. The name refers to the roughly 80,000 hours a typical person works over their lifetime. It publishes an evidence-based career guide, in-depth problem profiles, a long-form podcast, and one-on-one advising, and runs a curated high-impact job board at jobs.80000hours.org. Since 2016 it has ranked helping navigate the transition to advanced AI as its top priority. It is a content and career-advice organization rather than an API producer; no public developer API is published, though it does serve a machine-readable llms.txt index of its content.

providers.name: Academia
providers.description: Academia (Academia.edu, Academia Inc.) is a San Francisco based platform for sharing and discovering academic research, founded in 2008 by Richard Price. Registered researchers upload papers, build public profiles, follow research interests and track readership analytics across a corpus of tens of millions of documents, and the company also runs the Academia journals program and sells Academia Premium subscriptions for advanced search, mentions, reader analytics and bulk PDF downloads. Academia publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the /v0 JSON endpoints its own web client calls are explicitly disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt. It does publish an RFC 9116 security.txt with a named security contact and a disclosure posture, and a long per-crawler robots.txt that names AI and agent user-agents individually.

providers.name: Brit + Co
providers.description: Brit + Co is a lifestyle and entertainment media platform founded by Brit Morin that publishes content and creative education for a primarily women audience. It covers self-care, food, home and DIY, travel, relationships, celebrity and entertainment news, horoscopes, shopping guides, and games, and operates a learning platform (learn.brit.co) offering more than one hundred creative online classes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures. It is a consumer media and e-learning brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Incluyeme
providers.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities. Its online platform connects candidates with disabilities to inclusive employers, offering job listings, virtual training courses, scholarships, and mentorship for individuals, alongside inclusive-hiring consulting, talent sourcing, staff training, and physical/web accessibility evaluation for companies. Operating across roughly a dozen countries in Latin America (Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico, Uruguay, Paraguay and more), it has registered hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities and placed thousands into roles with 100+ corporate clients. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Pensive
providers.description: Pensive is an AI grading platform for educators at schools and universities. Its "AI Grader" helps instructors evaluate student work — grading assignments and returning feedback at scale — alongside an AI tutor product for students. Pensive serves distinct teacher, student, and administrator surfaces, publishes case studies with university instructors, and maintains a SOC 2 trust center. It is a seed-stage company backed by Mayfield. As of this profiling Pensive operates a private, authenticated web product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Quizlet
providers.description: Quizlet is a San Francisco-based global learning platform offering flashcards, practice tests, and AI-powered study tools used by students, teachers, and lifelong learners. Core features include user-created and expert-verified study sets, Learn mode (adaptive practice), Test mode, Match game, Spaced Repetition, and an AI tutor (Q-Chat / Magic Notes) that generates flashcards, summaries, practice questions, and explanations from uploaded notes, PDFs, slides, and textbooks. Quizlet Plus is the company's consumer subscription, and Quizlet for Schools / Teachers provides licensed offerings for classrooms. The platform integrates with Google Classroom (share-as-assignment) and Canvas (embeddable widgets) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK — the legacy Developer API 2.0 (`quizlet.com/api/2.0`) was effectively wound down to partners-only and is not openly registrable. Quizlet's GitHub organization (`github.com/quizlet`) hosts internal tooling, GitHub Actions, and forks of OSS dependencies (HHVM/Hack, PHPUnit, Mockery, Stylus, etc.) rather than a developer-facing API platform.

providers.name: QuEra Computing
providers.description: QuEra Computing is a Boston-area neutral-atom quantum computing company, founded in 2021 by scientists from Harvard and MIT. Its flagship system, Aquila, is a 256-qubit field-programmable analog neutral-atom quantum processor that has been publicly available since November 2022 through Amazon Braket and through a direct Premium Access channel. QuEra develops Bloqade, an open-source software stack for neutral-atom quantum computing delivered as a Python SDK (Bloqade Python) and as the original Bloqade.jl Julia package, along with surrounding tooling for circuits, analog control, atom shuttling, decoders, and tensor-network simulation. The company is building toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with its Gemini-class next-generation systems and has demonstrated logical-level magic state distillation on neutral-atom hardware. QuEra works with HPC centers, national labs (NERSC, Los Alamos), DARPA, NEDO/AIST, NVIDIA, AWS, BCG X, Deloitte, Classiq, Kipu Quantum, Wolfram Research, and enterprise customers including BP, BASF, Merck, and Amgen. The system is consumed via the Bloqade SDK or AWS Braket; QuEra does not currently expose a public REST API to its QPU.

providers.name: Bloom Institute of Technology
providers.description: Bloom Institute of Technology (formerly Lambda School) is an online coding bootcamp founded in 2017 that trains learners for AI-driven tech careers through part-time and full-time programs in Full Stack Web Development, Backend Development, and Data Science, plus corporate "AI for Developer Productivity" training. It is known for its income-share and deferred-tuition model ($0 upfront with a job-contingent payment plan) and a tuition-refund guarantee. The company reports 4,000+ graduates since 2017. It is a venture-backed consumer education company (backed by GV) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Clanbeat
providers.description: Clanbeat is an Estonian education-technology company whose app supports student and staff well-being by nurturing social and emotional learning (SEL) through co-creation. The platform provides well-being tracking, quality reflections, meaningful connections between students and educators, and tools to co-create SEL curriculum. It is used by international schools, educators, students, and fitness and lifelong-learning communities to evidence group emotional well-being and bring classes closer together. Clanbeat is delivered as a hosted web and mobile application at app.clanbeat.com; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or partner integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Conicle
providers.description: Conicle is a Thai education-technology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Bangkok that offers an all-in-one corporate learning platform (ConicleX) letting organizations build, assign, and track online courses, in-house training, and skill-development pathways for their employees. The cloud-based learning management system serves more than 50 leading enterprises — including Honda, Coca-Cola, Unilever, McDonald's, Sansiri, and The Mall — and over one million learners across the banking, retail, healthcare, energy, insurance, and consumer-product sectors. Conicle has raised Series A funding led by InVent (the corporate venture arm of Intouch Holdings), with backing from 500 Global and Stormbreaker Ventures. Conicle publishes a shared design-system web-components library used across its properties but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Liveboard
providers.description: LiveBoard is a tutor-management platform that helps tutoring businesses, academies, and independent tutors run their operations end to end. It combines branded virtual classrooms (video calls, screen sharing, an interactive whiteboard, recording, and file sharing) with session scheduling and attendance tracking, tutor/student/parent management, calendar-based billing with online payments, auto-invoicing, payroll, and progress reporting. Liveboard says it serves 200,000+ tutors and companies across 200+ countries, scaling from solo tutors to organizations with thousands of tutors. It is a consumer/SaaS product with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time; integrations are teaching-focused (Wacom pen tablets, a LaTeX formula editor, and the Desmos graphing calculator). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Melodics
providers.description: Melodics is a New Zealand-based interactive music-learning application that teaches drums, MIDI keyboards, and pad controllers (finger drumming) through gamified, real-time lessons. It connects to electronic instruments and MIDI controllers to give immediate feedback on timing and accuracy, offering guided learning paths, song tutorials, and structured daily practice for beginner through advanced players across desktop and mobile. Melodics is a consumer edtech product and a portfolio company of 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: PLOS
providers.description: These examples use the search API to search the PLOS corpus of scientific articles. These examples are not intended to be a full explanation on the use of Solr. A full Solr query language explanation can be found here and a tutorial here. The construction of PLOS search queries deviates from the standard Solr query URL by using search instead of select when making request to the end point. The primary endpoint is http://api.plos.org/search and supports parameters such as q, fl, wt, start, and rows for querying the PLOS Solr index.

providers.name: Solvely Ai
providers.description: Solvely is an all-in-one AI study platform for students from K-12 through graduate level, trusted by more than 10 million students across 5,000+ universities worldwide. It combines multi-model homework help with step-by-step solutions, an AI note taker that transcribes lectures into structured notes, a quiz maker, an essay writer, math and equation solvers (algebra, geometry, calculus, statistics), auto-generated flashcards and study guides, mock exams, an exam predictor, and cheat sheets. Solvely is available on the web, iOS, Android, and as a Chrome/Edge browser extension, with free and paid (Solvely Unlimited) tiers. It is a consumer-facing product and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Cometa
providers.description: Cometa (getcometa.com / cometaedu.com) is a Mexican education technology company that provides an operating system for private schools. More than 500 private schools in Mexico use Cometa to run and automate their operations across a set of integrated modules: Cobranzas (tuition collections with WhatsApp and email payment reminders and dashboards), Tienda en linea (an online store for uniforms, materials and services with vendor management), Admisiones y Reinscripciones (admissions and re-enrollment workflows), Comunicaciones (AI-assisted, multi-channel family communications with engagement analytics), Calificaciones (grade entry and SEP-compliant report cards and digital credentials), and Gestion Escolar (attendance, incident logging and administrative workflows). Cometa is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was surfaced as a stub in the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Cometa publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

providers.name: Mattilda
providers.description: Mattilda is a financial management platform for private educational institutions across Latin America, operating in Mexico, Colombia, and Ecuador. It automates tuition collection and payment processing, offers tuition advances that guarantee schools receive full monthly tuition on the first day regardless of family payment rates, and provides academic operations and admissions tools under its Algebraix product line. Families can pay through multiple channels, including WhatsApp. Mattilda operates under the oversight of Mexico's financial authorities CNBV and CONDUSEF and is backed by QED Investors. Mattilda does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation portal; this profile captures the company's public identity, status page, and Vanta-hosted trust center.

providers.name: Edison Scientific
providers.description: Edison Scientific is an AI research company building Kosmos, an autonomous "AI Scientist" for R&D teams in drug discovery and biopharma. Kosmos reads scientific literature, analyzes experimental data, generates and tests hypotheses, and executes research workflows autonomously, collaborating with scientists through tools like Slack and Teams. The model-agnostic platform spans the drug development lifecycle from target identification through clinical development and filing, learning from proprietary organizational and scientific data. Edison Labs publishes open science research including the PaperQA line of multimodal deep research agents. The company is backed by Spark Capital and maintains an enterprise Trust Center with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture. No public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: Open Mainframe Project
providers.description: The Open Mainframe Project is a Linux Foundation project encouraging the use of Linux-based operating systems and open source software on mainframe computers. Founded in 2015 with IBM, it hosts projects such as Zowe (modern interfaces for z/OS), Feilong (z/VM cloud connector), Galasa (testing), and a range of community programs that promote mainframe skills and open source on IBM Z and LinuxONE platforms.

providers.name: US Capitol Visitor Center
providers.description: The US Capitol Visitor Center (CVC) serves as the main entrance for visitors to the United States Capitol, providing resources and information to enhance the visitor experience. The Center offers guided tours of the Capitol building, allowing visitors to explore the historic rooms and learn about the legislative process. It also houses exhibits and educational materials that highlight the history and significance of the Capitol and its role in American democracy. The CVC operates under the Architect of the Capitol and offers free guided tours, specialty tours, virtual tours, and educational programs for students and visitors from around the world.

providers.name: Coursebase
providers.description: Coursebase is an AI-powered corporate Learning Management System (LMS) used by over 1,000 organizations to create, deliver, and manage employee training across online, in-person, and blended formats. The platform offers a library of 1,000+ pre-built eLearning courses, AI-assisted content generation (auto-generated test questions and course summaries), analytics and reporting dashboards, single sign-on, multi-language support, and API-based integration with external HR systems for syncing user account information. Coursebase was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched in the API Evangelist network; the public surface is a marketing site with an enterprise "contact us" API integration offering rather than a self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI.

providers.name: Chegg
providers.description: Chegg is an American education technology company that provides direct-to-student learning services, including 24/7 homework and expert Q&A help, step-by-step textbook solutions, practice questions, and writing, grammar, and citation tools. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Chegg began as a textbook-rental marketplace and expanded into a subscription study-support platform (Chegg Study, Chegg Writing, Chegg Math Solver) plus tutoring and skills offerings. Chegg operates as a consumer web/mobile product rather than a developer platform: it exposes no public developer portal, published API, or SDKs at this time. Its public technical surface is limited to a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program on HackerOne and standard web security/policy pages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Fizz
providers.description: Fizz is a social platform built for college campuses, connecting students within their own school communities across 700+ campuses in the United States. Founded by Stanford students, Fizz gives verified students an anonymous, hyper-local feed to find their community and join the conversation, buy and sell through Fizz Marketplace, and engage under community values of being supportive, curious, honest, and brave. The platform is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and NEA. Fizz is a consumer mobile social app and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface for network discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Geniebook
providers.description: Geniebook is a Singapore-based educational technology company (Geniebook Pte Ltd, incorporated 2016) offering an AI-powered online learning platform for primary, secondary, and JC students. Its product suite includes GenieSmart (AI-personalised worksheets generated from a library of 300,000+ MOE syllabus-aligned questions, using algorithms co-developed with A*STAR), GenieClass (live and recorded online classes taught by experienced teachers), and GenieAsk (real-time moderated teacher chats for after-school academic support), plus a CAMPUS physical-tutoring offering and PSLE/JC preparation programmes. Geniebook serves more than 220,000 students across Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer (B2C) learning application delivered via web and mobile apps; no public developer API is published.

providers.name: Lica
providers.description: Lica is an AI research company building a substrate to train and evaluate AI models to be capable design partners across expressions of taste and consumption. Its research spans spatial reasoning and composition, layout generation and editing, vector-graphics (SVG) understanding, personalization and brand identity, and animation generation. Lica publishes the LICA dataset of layered graphic-design compositions and GDB (Graphic Design Benchmark), a real-world benchmark that scores frontier models on designer workflows across layout, typography, infographics, template semantics and animation. The company is backed by Accel, South Park Commons and Village Global. As of July 2026 Lica ships no public API, developer portal or API reference; product access is an email waitlist and its public developer surface is the lica-world GitHub organization, including the first-party DesignMCP MCP server.

providers.name: BridgeU
providers.description: BridgeU is an education technology company providing a university and careers guidance platform for international schools. Used by more than 1,200 partner schools across 150+ countries, the platform helps students from Grade 9 onward explore careers, research over 26,000 global universities, build shortlists, and manage applications in one connected system, with analytics dashboards for counsellors and AI-assisted guidance. BridgeU is a Seedcamp portfolio company and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery surface as of this enrichment pass; integration with school systems (for example ManageBac+) is handled via partner single sign-on rather than an openly documented API.

providers.name: GrowthHackers
providers.description: GrowthHackers (Growth Hackers Company, LLC) is a growth-marketing community and software company built around the growth-hacking discipline Sean Ellis named. It runs an invite-only community for founders, heads of growth, marketers and product managers, publishes growth research, case studies, opinion pieces and the State of Growth survey, and hosts webinars, AMAs and a conference. Alongside the community it sells growth and AI marketing services and ships Growth OS, an AI-powered growth and optimization platform for agencies that combines experiment planning, content creation, digital marketing execution and reporting. GrowthHackers publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Leland
providers.description: Leland is a marketplace for ambitious people to access the coaching, classes, and community they need to reach career and educational goals. It connects individuals with vetted 1-on-1 coaches across MBA and college admissions, management consulting, investment banking, private equity, product management, law, medicine, and executive and career development, and sells structured live programs, bootcamps, and test prep for the GMAT, GRE, LSAT, MCAT, SAT, and ACT. Leland+ is a subscription content library of video guides, essay and resume examples, templates, and expert-built AI tools. For organizations Leland offers AI-native talent training, agentic workflow deployment, recruiting, and outplacement, plus university and HR partnerships. Leland publishes no public API or developer portal as of 2026-07-19.

providers.name: Lendorse
providers.description: Lendorse GmbH is a Berlin-based education-finance company that funds international master's students studying in Europe through Income Share Agreements (ISAs) instead of traditional credit-scored loans. Students receive between EUR 3,000 and EUR 20,000 toward tuition, visa deposits, relocation and living costs, then repay a fixed 6-12% share of gross monthly income for 12 to 60 months once they earn above a EUR 2,500 monthly salary floor, with total repayment capped at 2.3x the funded amount. No collateral, co-signer, parental guarantor or credit check is required, which opens funding to students from developing and emerging markets who are normally excluded. Lendorse also provides mentorship, CV review, mock interviews and industry introductions. It covers universities in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland, went through the Techstars and ABN AMRO Future of Finance Accelerator, and raised EUR 1.75M co-led by LUMO Labs and Soulmates Ventures. Lendorse publishes no public API, SDKs or developer portal as of July 2026; this profile is a company record rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Torch
providers.description: Torch (Redfish Labs, Inc. dba Torch Leadership Labs) is a leadership development and executive coaching platform that pairs expert human coaches with AI to help mid-market and enterprise organizations grow leaders and navigate change. Its offerings include Change Coaching (leaders-turned-coaches trained in Torch's change approach), the Spark AI coaching agent (always-on AI guidance for practicing conversations and turning insight into progress), and Organizational Intelligence (real-time visibility into change patterns and people dynamics). Torch focuses on AI transformation, organizational restructuring, organizational resilience, and leadership growth, and counts Airbnb, Reddit, Tripadvisor, FICO, and Twitch among its customers. Torch is a SaaS product with SSO (SAML), Zoom, and Slack integrations but publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Corca
providers.description: Corca is an AI-native, collaborative workspace for mathematics — a browser-based editor that lets people write math naturally (without special syntax), run calculations in real time, and collaborate the way teams do in Figma or Google Docs. Typing keywords like "sum" or "integral" surfaces the right symbols and functions, documents import from and export to LaTeX, and built-in AI helps solve problems, manipulate expressions, and generate code without switching tools. It is used for lab research, lecture creation, team knowledge bases, and publishing academic work. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Corca raised a $7.8M round (led by NEA, with Bloomberg Beta, NVIDIA's NVentures, Daft Capital, Slow Ventures, Liquid 2, Path Ventures, and Mana Ventures). The product is a consumer/team SaaS application; no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Nookly
providers.description: Nookly is a personalized children's content platform that helps the adults who care for a child — parents, teachers, therapists, and early-childhood organizations — turn their intimate knowledge of that child into custom stories, songs, visual schedules, social stories, emotion cards, and behavior supports. Grounded in social-emotional learning and behavioral science, it produces developmentally appropriate, COPPA/FERPA-compliant content for children ages 2-11, with particular value for neurodivergent kids (autism, ADHD, speech delays, anxiety, and sensory processing differences). Used across homes, classrooms, and clinics in 50+ states.

providers.name: Imperfect
providers.description: Imperfect (Imperfect Wellness, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) consumer startup building an adaptive AI training coach for endurance athletes across cycling, trail running, swimming, and other sports. The mobile app connects to a user's wearables and health apps to generate real-time training, recovery, and nutrition recommendations that adapt to how the athlete's body is actually responding day to day, rather than following a static plan written weeks in advance. Founded by Matin Tamizi (previously built and sold two fintech companies and authored a widely used open-source Garmin library used by Stanford Health). Imperfect ships as a consumer mobile application (Google Play) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Admittedly
providers.description: myOptions (myoptions.org redirects to encourageme.com; operated as the Encourage platform by Encoura, LLC) is a free college and career planning platform for middle- and high-school students, families, and educators across the United States. Students explore colleges, majors, careers, and scholarships and get matched to institutions, while educators deliver guidance through lesson plans, preference forms, and reporting dashboards. The platform reports serving roughly 4 million students across 5,000 school districts and 10,000+ high schools in all 50 states and D.C., funded through partnerships with colleges and education providers rather than user fees. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation surface, and no real /.well-known/ documents (all such paths return the SPA/404 catch-all). Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead under the stub slug 'admittedly'.

providers.name: doinstruct
providers.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

providers.name: Kibin
providers.description: Kibin is a consumer study and academic-writing company operating at kibin.com, trusted by students since 2011. Its newest product is an AI-powered study partner (iOS app) that turns lectures, notes, PDFs, and YouTube videos into personalized study guides, quizzes, flashcards, transcripts, and explanations to help students learn faster and build mastery. Alongside the study app, Kibin also runs its long-standing academic-writing surface — professional essay editing, a paper grader, a thesis-statement generator, essay examples, and a writing blog. Kibin is a B2C, mobile- and web-delivered product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Manara
providers.description: Manara is an upskilling and professional development platform focused on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, specializing in training for emerging technologies including AI and cloud computing. It runs enterprise workforce-development programs, national government training initiatives, and individual learning and certification courses, connecting a community of MENA software engineers and technologists with global career opportunities. The company reports 300,000+ learners trained, 2,500+ certifications awarded, operations across 40+ countries, and 500+ job placements. Manara publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Marcopolo Learning
providers.description: MarcoPolo Learning is an award-winning early childhood education technology company, founded in 2013, that builds premium video content, instructional support, and learning apps for preschool and kindergarten. Its products include MarcoPolo For Educators (curriculum-aligned classroom video and educator guides), MarcoPolo For Families (Emmy-nominated videos plus literacy and math games), MarcoPolo World School (kindergarten readiness), MarcoPolo Professional Development for teachers, and The Polos animated series. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MarcoPolo Learning publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable developer surface; it is a consumer/educator app business, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Novel Effect
providers.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SplashLearn
providers.description: SplashLearn (operated by StudyPad, Inc.) is a game-based learning platform offering math and English/ELA curriculum for preschool through Grade 5 students, used by parents, teachers, schools, and homeschoolers. It delivers interactive games, worksheets, lesson plans, and progress tracking across web and mobile (iOS/Android) apps, plus homeschool, summer-learning, and SpringBoard programs. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web/security surface.

providers.name: The Learning Experience
providers.description: The Learning Experience is an early childhood education and childcare franchise operating academies of early education for children from six weeks to six years old across a nationwide network of centers. Its programs span infant, toddler, preschool, and pre-kindergarten care built on a proprietary curriculum. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer-facing childcare operator it publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: Cambly
providers.description: Cambly is an online English-language learning platform, founded in 2012 and based in San Francisco, that connects English learners in more than 190 countries with native-speaking tutors over on-demand video chat. Its consumer products include Cambly (adult learners), Cambly Kids (ages 4-15), Cambly Pro, and Cambly for Organizations/Business. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, and Y Combinator, the company operates a marketplace connecting students and tutors with weekly payouts. Cambly does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public company surface, GitHub organization, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Ideal Invest
providers.description: Ideal Invest (operating as Pravaler) is a Brazilian fintech founded in 2002 and headquartered in Sao Paulo that provides private student financing for higher education. Through its Pravaler platform, students can split tuition payments across roughly twice the duration of a course, with a 100% digital, low-bureaucracy application, competitive monthly interest rates, and no ENEM requirement. Pravaler works with a network of 500+ partner higher-education institutions and has financed more than 400,000 students, channeling over R$12 billion into Brazilian education. The company is backed by Ribbit Capital. As of this enrichment pass Pravaler exposes a consumer web platform (simulation, application, digital signature) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: Piazza
providers.description: Piazza is an online question-and-answer platform for higher education that connects students, teaching assistants, and professors in a single wiki-style collaborative space for each class. Instructors run a Piazza for their course where students ask and answer questions, post anonymously, use a LaTeX and code editor for technical content, and receive instructor-endorsed answers. Piazza integrates with every major learning management system (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Sakai, Desire2Learn, and others) via the LTI standard for single-click class creation, roster-based automatic enrollment, and automatic single sign-on. It is used across thousands of universities in more than 90 countries and is FERPA-compliant. Piazza does not publish an official public developer API; LMS connectivity is delivered through LTI, and only community projects wrap its internal endpoints.

providers.name: EverTrue
providers.description: EverTrue is a donor experience and fundraising platform for nonprofit, higher-education, and healthcare advancement teams, serving more than 13,000 teams. Its product suite spans AI-driven prospect identification and research (Signal, DonorSearch), donor outreach and stewardship (ThankView personalized video, Pledgemine direct mail), and endowment reporting (Balance, Impact, ODDER). EverTrue integrates with advancement CRMs such as Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT via an automated data sync. EverTrue operates as a closed B2B SaaS: it runs internal REST APIs behind its iOS, Android, and single-page web applications but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API program. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: Goodfellow
providers.description: Goodfellow (Goodfellow Advanced Materials) is a global specialty-materials supplier founded in 1946 and headquartered in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, serving research, prototyping and specialized manufacturing markets in more than 111 countries. Its catalog spans over 70,000 stocked products drawn from 700+ different materials in many forms, including metals, alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites, compounds and glass, alongside custom fabrication and laboratory testing services. Customers include universities, government research facilities, laboratories and advanced manufacturers, served through subsidiaries in the United States, China, France and Germany. Goodfellow was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2021 to help digitize its operations and fund materials acquisitions. Goodfellow is a business-to-business e-commerce and catalog operation; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks.

providers.name: Skillshare
providers.description: Skillshare is a New York City–based online learning community for creators, founded in 2010 by Michael Karnjanaprakorn and Malcolm Ong. The platform hosts thousands of on-demand video classes across creative disciplines — illustration, design, photography, animation, lettering, film, productivity, writing, and business — taught by working creators and industry professionals. Skillshare operates on a paid subscription model (Premium membership) that grants members unlimited access to the class catalog, project-based learning, and a discussion community where students submit class projects for feedback. The company has a teacher revenue-share program in which class creators are paid based on watch time and student enrollments, and runs Skillshare for Teams as a B2B offering for organizations to give employees access to the catalog. Skillshare does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner API, or SDK. The platform's programmatic surface is limited to internal web/mobile clients and an affiliate/marketing referral program; there is no documented developer portal, public webhook system, or third-party integration API for the Skillshare catalog, enrollments, watch-time, or teacher-payout data.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: Successfactors
providers.description: SuccessFactors is a cloud-based human capital management (HCM) company founded in 2001 and an early Canaan Partners portfolio company that IPO'd in 2007 and was acquired by SAP in 2012. It is now delivered as the SAP SuccessFactors HXM (Human Experience Management) Suite, covering core HR (Employee Central), Recruiting, Onboarding, Performance & Goals, Compensation, Learning (LMS), Succession & Development, and Workforce Analytics. SuccessFactors exposes an extensive integration surface through OData v2 and OData v4 APIs (the SFAPI/OData platform) documented on the SAP Business Accelerator Hub, using OAuth 2.0 SAML bearer-assertion and basic authentication per customer datacenter instance.

providers.name: Chinese Medicine Online
providers.description: Chinese Medicine Online (中医在线) is a Beijing-based traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) continuing-education and academic-exchange platform, founded in 2015 and operated by Beijing Universe In Nutshell Technology Co., Ltd. (北京果壳宇宙教育科技有限公司) on behalf of the Beijing TCM Online Education Center (北京中医在线教育中心). Through its web platform at tcmmooc.com and its iOS/Android app, it publishes recorded and live video continuing-education courses from national TCM masters and senior practitioners, runs the 经方学社 (Classical Formulas Society) learning community and 精医社 membership, livestreams academic conferences, and sells course material through a paid knowledge marketplace. The company states a catalogue of roughly 19,600 courses from 3,900+ TCM experts and around 4 million registered users, the majority of them licensed practitioners. It has since extended into AI and SaaS for grassroots clinics, including the "Yi Yin" (伊尹) TCM classical-reasoning large language model launched in Songxian, Henan in September 2025, and clinic workflow tooling (prescription, patient and follow-up management). The platform is delivered strictly as an end-user web and mobile product — it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Citruslabs
providers.description: Citruslabs is a clinical research organization (CRO) that designs and runs clinical trials, consumer perception studies, and randomized controlled trials for consumer health brands across supplements, skincare, pet health, food and beverage, longevity, and women's health. It handles IRB approval, protocol design, participant recruitment, decentralized data collection, and statistical analysis, then turns results into regulator-reviewed, marketing-ready product claims for retailers, advertising, and packaging. Studies range from DIY consumer perception studies to full randomized controlled trials, typically completing in four to sixteen weeks.

providers.name: Conceive
providers.description: Conceive is a telehealth platform for fertility and pregnancy support. It offers 24/7 text access to fertility and pregnancy nurses, coaches, and dietitians, personalized fertility coaching, fertility test interpretation, virtual video visits with providers, expert-led community events, and an educational library. Membership is delivered through Conceive Plus and Conceive Premium tiers. The company is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. As a consumer telehealth app it publishes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its published identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Ethos Systems
providers.description: Ethos Systems is an AI-powered human readiness platform that unifies learning, performance, and outcomes management in a single system built for enterprise and government deployment across both commercial and classified networks. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Ethos delivers personalized training with algorithm-driven interventions, rapid AI content development, and real-time readiness dashboards that connect learning to operational outcomes. It serves the U.S. military, federal civilian agencies, life sciences, manufacturing, freight and logistics, hospitality, athletics, utilities, insurance, and government contractors, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the Westly Group, and Pear VC. The company operates the Ethos and Learn to Win platforms; its developer and product documentation is gated behind authentication and it exposes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Ello
providers.description: Ello is a public-benefit AI education company building a 1:1 AI reading and math tutor for children ages 4-9. Its consumer app pairs proprietary child-speech recognition (trained on 100K+ hours of kids' audio) with generative AI and adaptive teaching agents to deliver personalized, sub-second, voice-based reading instruction grounded in the Science of Reading, plus a large catalog of leveled e-books, a "Storytime" create-your-own story feature, and parent progress reports. Recognized as one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2024 and backed by Y Combinator, Goodwater, Project A, and Homebrew, Ello is a consumer (B2C) product with no public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Hyperpad
providers.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

providers.name: LabLabee
providers.description: LabLabee is an AI-powered enablement, testing and troubleshooting platform for telecom teams, positioning itself as "the Copilot for Telco Engineers." The platform delivers on-demand, hands-on labs, sandboxes, learning paths and skill tests covering 4G/5G and Open RAN, IMS, network OAM, SDN and IP networking, telco cloud (OpenStack, OpenShift, Kubernetes, Docker), DevOps and GitOps automation (Terraform, Ansible, CI/CD), Linux, IAM and cybersecurity, and Industry 4.0 and IoT. Three AI capabilities sit on top of the lab catalog: AI Ask (search across telecom standards, vendor documentation and enterprise knowledge), AI Test (automated test execution and configuration validation) and AI Troubleshoot (automated trace analysis and root-cause identification). LabLabee serves telcos, universities, system integrators, network vendors and industrial private-network operators. Founded by Samir Tahraoui (CEO) and Mahfoud S. A. Mebarek (CPO), the company is backed by Accel, Kima Ventures, Reach Capital, Brighteye Ventures and 500 Global, and has been recognized as Best Telecom Startup by the World Communication Awards and with the TM Forum Growth Challenge Award. As of this enrichment pass LabLabee publishes no public developer program - no API documentation, API reference, OpenAPI, SDKs, CLI or public package artifacts were found on any of its surfaces.

providers.name: On Deck
providers.description: On Deck (now operating as the On Deck Founder Fellowship, ODF) is a founder fellowship and startup community program that helps aspiring entrepreneurs start companies through an intense, in-person cohort experience focused on meeting co-founders, exploring ideas, and gaining conviction. Backed by Canaan Partners, On Deck provides mentorship, a peer community, and startup perks. It is a program and community platform rather than a developer or API product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sidechat
providers.description: Sidechat is an anonymous, campus-based social networking app for college students, built by Flower Ave Inc in New York City and backed by Canaan Partners.
