Students verify with a school email to join their college's private, location- and campus-scoped community where they post text, images, and polls, vote, and chat anonymously in a Reddit-like feed. Sidechat launched in early 2022, acquired Yik Yak in 2023, and operates primarily as an iOS consumer app. It publishes no official public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures the company's public web presence and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sphero
providers.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

providers.name: Track Titan
providers.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

providers.name: Zoog
providers.description: Zoog is a consumer mobile app platform that lets families create and share personalized video books and songs for children. Users read classic kids' stories or sing popular kids' songs while the app adds filters, effects, and music to produce custom animated videos that connect loved ones across distances. Founded in 2021 by Yoav Oren and Matan Guttman and backed by Techstars, Zoog is used by families worldwide. It is a consumer product with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: AOne
providers.description: AOne is a Malaysia-based learning-centre management software company (operating publicly as AOneSchools) whose all-in-one platform is used by 4,000+ tuition centres, preschools, enrichment centres, sports academies, and language centres to automate billing, LHDN e-invoicing, attendance tracking, student and class management, and parent communication across connected web and mobile apps. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. The company's public surface today is a marketing website (aone.com.my) and a customer login/app at app.aoneschools.com; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or /.well-known discovery surface is currently published.

providers.name: Cajal Technologies
providers.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

providers.name: ClassWallet
providers.description: ClassWallet is a patented digital wallet and public-funds disbursement platform used by government agencies, school districts, and program administrators to distribute, control, and reconcile public money. Recipients access and spend allocated funds online or in-store while administrators get spending controls, approved marketplaces, reimbursement workflows, direct vendor payments (DirectPay), and audit-ready reporting and compliance. ClassWallet powers K-12 education programs, Education Savings Accounts (ESAs), scholarships and grants, government assistance, and vocational rehabilitation initiatives. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes product and program surfaces but no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Emeritus
providers.description: Emeritus is a global online education company that partners with more than 80 premier universities — including Wharton, MIT, Columbia, Harvard, Kellogg, and UC Berkeley — to deliver outcome-based executive education, professional certificates, and skill-development programs to over 500,000 learners worldwide. It operates across individual learners, enterprise/corporate training, and university-branded partnership programs, spanning topics such as AI and machine learning, data science, finance, leadership, and digital transformation through instructor-led online and blended formats. Emeritus is backed by Accel and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Emeritus publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Icon Source
providers.description: Icon Source is a Denver, Colorado marketplace that connects brands, marketing agencies and universities with professional and college athletes for endorsement, appearance, speaking and social-media deals, including Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) engagements. Founded in 2018 by Chase Garrett, the platform lets brands search and filter verified athletes by location, interest, rate, audience size and demographics, build and send contracts, and pay athletes in-platform, charging a 10% transaction fee on each deal that is signed and closed. A companion product, Icon Suite (launched March 2022), gives universities NIL disclosure and compliance tooling. Icon Source is delivered strictly as an end-user product — a web application at prod.iconsource.app plus iOS and Android apps — and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Linguatrip
providers.description: Linguatrip is a language-education and language-travel company founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global. It operates two connected businesses: a booking marketplace for accredited language schools abroad — covering course selection, accommodation, airport transfers and visa support across countries including the United Kingdom, Malta and the United Arab Emirates — and its own online English school offering 25+ self-paced courses, one-to-one tutoring, speaking clubs and exam preparation for IELTS, TOEFL, GMAT, GRE and SAT. It also provides higher-education placement consulting for US, UK and Canadian universities. Linguatrip publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; its surfaces are consumer web properties in four languages with pricing in 18 currencies.

providers.name: PlanetSpark
providers.description: PlanetSpark is an Indian education-technology company headquartered in Gurugram, founded in 2017 by Kunal Malik and Maneesh Dhooper, that delivers live 1:1 online classes in public speaking, spoken English, creative writing, grammar, debating and vlogging to K-8 learners, along with mental and Vedic mathematics, abacus and school-excellence programmes, plus communication courses for working professionals. It sells directly to parents and learners through www.planetspark.in as a consumer subscription; it operates no public developer programme, publishes no API documentation or machine-readable contract, and its only external integration surface is an affiliate registration programme.

providers.name: Sonar Mental Health
providers.description: Sonar Mental Health provides 24/7 text-based wellbeing coaching and care navigation for youth. Trained Wellbeing Coaches lead the conversations, supported by AI tooling that surfaces context and flags risk without making independent decisions, delivering between-visit and after-hours support, escalation and care coordination to higher levels of care, and real-time insights dashboards for measurement-based care across schools, health systems, primary care, and EAP pathways. The company reports serving 20,000+ young people with higher engagement between visits, and is backed by 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture (SOC 2, HIPAA), and public web properties.

providers.name: Upkid
providers.description: Upkid is a childcare staffing marketplace that connects early childhood programs such as daycares and preschools with qualified, pre-vetted substitute and full-time teachers. Programs post shifts and roles while educators find flexible teaching opportunities through the Upkid web and mobile apps, with an ATS-style Hiring Hub for full-time childcare hiring. Upkid operates across metro areas in Georgia, Utah, and Arizona and is a Techstars portfolio company. Upkid publishes no public API or developer portal; its web app is a client of a Firebase backend.

providers.name: Atypical AI
providers.description: Atypical AI is an artificial-intelligence and learning-science lab building generative-AI learning products for educators, learners, and content creators. Its flagship product, ExamJam, is an AI tutor that pairs adaptive, personalized tutoring with trusted exam content from major publishers (Pearson, McGraw Hill, Collins) to help students prepare for and revise toward their exams. Founded in 2023 and based in San Francisco, the woman-owned company builds personalized tutoring, exam preparation, content creation, collaboration, and student-success measurement tools grounded in learning science. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta; it publishes a consumer product surface (web + mobile) and no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Greator
providers.description: Greator (formerly GEDANKENtanken, founded 2012) is Germany's largest personal- development platform, headquartered in Cologne and serving roughly 234,000 customers. It runs a B2C ecosystem of free content (masterclasses, podcasts, a YouTube channel, magazine articles and personality tests) alongside paid, certified training programs such as The School of Life, Momentum Mastery, the Finance Academy and TheKey speaking training. Greator also produces live events including the annual Greator Festival (15,000+ attendees, 400+ speakers) and operates Greator Business, a B2B corporate offering. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Greator publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: LF Research
providers.description: LF Research is the Linux Foundation's research arm that publishes reports and studies on open source trends, OSPO practices, technology adoption, and industry analysis. It provides data-driven insights to help organizations understand and participate in open source ecosystems.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: One Month
providers.description: One Month is an online coding education platform that teaches beginners practical software and web development skills through short, project-based video courses designed to be completed in about a month. Its catalog spans programming languages and frameworks such as Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, HTML & CSS, SQL, and WordPress, alongside professional skills like project management, using a "watch, do, repeat" methodology of hands-on lessons and follow-along projects. One Month markets itself to career changers and non-programmers looking to accelerate into technical roles, and publishes a supporting blog of programming tutorials and career guidance. It is a consumer-facing learning product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pandai
providers.description: Pandai is a Malaysian education technology company founded in 2020 that operates a digital learning platform for primary and secondary school students. The app aligns to Malaysia's national curriculum (DSKP) across KSSR Years 1-6 and KSSM Forms 1-5, including SPM exam preparation, and helps learners improve their grades through interactive quizzes, tests, exams, topical practice, notes, flashcards, videos, and live tutoring. Features include personalized assessments, an AI-powered revision assistant (Ask Pbot), gamified learning with battles, leaderboards and rewards, and performance tracking via scorecards and report cards. Pandai is a consumer-facing learning app and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Photomath
providers.description: Photomath is a mobile math-learning application that lets students scan a printed or handwritten math problem with their phone camera and returns step-by-step explanations, custom visual aids, and animated solving methods across topics from elementary arithmetic through calculus. Originally built by Croatian computer-vision company Microblink and later spun out as an independent education company backed by Menlo Ventures and Goldman Sachs, Photomath was acquired by Google in 2023 and now operates within Google (support is handled through Google's Help Center). It is a consumer subscription product distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play; it does not publish an official public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. The company previously stated it would not release a public Photomath SDK. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Menlo Ventures portfolio company and enriched to capture the company's public web and domain-security surface; no first-party API surface exists to catalog.

providers.name: Skool
providers.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

providers.name: Zzish
providers.description: Zzish is an EdTech company (a Techstars-backed startup) building a K-12 learning product suite used by teachers and students across 180 countries. Its flagship product, Quizalize, is a classroom quiz and formative-assessment platform; the portfolio also includes Blockerzz (a 3D game engine with quiz games and coding tutorials), Marvely.ai (AI-powered, exam-aligned language tutoring), Quizalize Insights (leadership dashboards for tracking academic progress), and QUAT (a customer-analytics platform for schools and EdTech partners). Zzish reports 250k+ teachers onboarded in the last two years and 250m+ questions answered since launch. As of this enrichment pass, Zzish publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer-documentation surface.

providers.name: Bloomy
providers.description: Bloomy (bloomylearning.com) is an AI-powered adaptive learning platform for K-12 students, founded by Alex Southmayd and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). The product diagnoses each student's knowledge gaps, builds a personalized standards-aligned learning path across English Language Arts, Math, and Writing, and delivers Socratic AI tutoring plus mastery-based practice, requiring 90%+ mastery before a student advances. It integrates third-party diagnostic/assessment data (i-Ready, NWEA MAP) and provides a real-time teacher dashboard. Bloomy serves traditional districts, charter schools, homeschools, and microschools, and sells to families via monthly or annual subscriptions (with ESA/EFA fund eligibility in some states). As of this profile Bloomy publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; this record captures its verified public identity and legal/account surface only.

providers.name: BridgeCare Finance
providers.description: BridgeCare (getbridgecare.com) is an integrated, modular software platform for the early care and education (ECE) system. It gives state agencies, cities and counties, child care resource and referral organizations (CCR&Rs), nonprofits, and school districts one system to run Pre-K program administration, family navigation, coordinated eligibility and enrollment, centralized eligibility screening, licensing, workforce development, quality management (QRIS), grants management, subsidy administration, tri-share administration, and program assurance. The platform is used by 500,000+ families, 50,000+ providers, and 500+ counties. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, BridgeCare is backed by Techstars and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. BridgeCare operates an API host but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer documentation, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Defense Technical Information Center
providers.description: The Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC) is the U.S. Department of Defense field activity that acquires, manages, and disseminates scientific and technical information from DoD-funded research, development, test, and evaluation. DTIC operates a public Research and Engineering (R&E) Gateway, the Discover service for searching technical reports, the DoDTechSpace and Minsky natural-language platforms for defense researchers, and Dimensions for collaborative discovery. Most DTIC services require authentication tied to DoD or registered-user roles. DTIC does not publicly publish a developer API, though tools such as Dimensions and Minsky offer programmatic capabilities to authorized users.

providers.name: Education Holdings 1 (The Princeton Review)
providers.description: Education Holdings 1 operates The Princeton Review, an educational services company offering standardized test preparation, one-on-one and on-demand tutoring, and college, graduate, medical, and law school admissions counseling. The Princeton Review prepares students for the SAT, ACT, PSAT, AP, MCAT, DAT, OAT, LSAT, GRE, GMAT, SSAT, ISEE, and SHSAT through live, self-paced, and honors courses, publishes college and graduate school rankings and guidebooks, and provides free practice tests, events, and study resources. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. The Princeton Review operates a consumer web presence rather than a public developer program; it publishes an llms.txt AI-discovery file but does not expose a documented public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: grasp
providers.description: Grasp is a members-based, AI-powered learning platform based in London, England that builds personalized, AI-curated short courses. Learners discuss a goal with an AI mentor, which co-creates a syllabus and assembles a structured "learning path" from the clearest, most credible resources on the web - organized into focused, roughly hour-long lessons with clear outcomes and practice exercises. Grasp is delivered as a client-rendered React single-page app with a 14-day free trial and a single monthly membership; a selection of public courses and lessons is browsable without an account, and a sister product, Grasp Concepts, lives at concepts.grasp.study. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and point-nine.

providers.name: Life is Tech
providers.description: Life is Tech, Inc. (ライフイズテック株式会社) is a Tokyo-based education technology company founded on 6 July 2010 by Yusuke Mizuno, delivering digital, programming and AI education to Japanese teenagers, schools, municipalities and employers. Its products are "Life is Tech !" IT camps and year-round schools for junior and senior high school students, "Life is Tech ! Lesson" — a cloud-based information and programming curriculum used by roughly 4,000 public and private schools across some 600 municipalities — "Life is Tech ! Leaders" for university students, "Life is Tech ! Career" digital job-hunting support, and DX Readiness corporate digital-skills training. The company is a certified B Corporation (October 2022, the first Japanese EdTech to certify) and holds the PrivacyMark. Life is Tech sells finished learning products to schools and consumers; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Mobilize
providers.description: Mobilize (mobilize.io) is a community and learning software platform purpose-built for associations and professional networks, now operating under the Forj brand (forj.ai). The platform unifies member community and continuing education in one place through its products Forj Connect (peer-to-peer and group member communication), Forj Learn (a learning management system for continuing education, certification, and social learning), and Journey by Forj (a combined community-and-learning experience). Mobilize was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a member/admin web application (app.mobilize.io) and a Zendesk help center but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so this profile carries verified company identity and link properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Play Versus
providers.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lagou
providers.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Mision Admision
providers.description: Misión Admisión is a Mexican education-technology company based in Mérida that prepares high school and university applicants for standardized admission exams such as EXANI I, EXANI II, PAA, and the UNAM, IPN, and UAM entrance tests. Its consumer web platform (misionadmision.com) delivers self-paced online courses, video lessons, interactive study capsules, thousands of practice questions, full-length exam simulators, live virtual and in-person classes, and the physical Sputnik smartbook guides. Founded in 2001 and online since 2015, the company is a seed-stage portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing EdTech platform and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Python Standard Library and Popular
providers.description: A collection of commonly used Python APIs and libraries including the standard library and popular frameworks like Flask, Django, FastAPI, Pandas, and NumPy.

providers.name: Chief
providers.description: Chief is a private membership network built to connect and support senior women leaders, serving executives across more than 10,000 companies with roughly 44% of members in C-suite roles. Membership combines vetted peer Core Groups, one-on-one and group executive coaching, business training (including programming with partners such as The Wharton School), member Clubhouses, and ChiefX events, plus an enterprise offering for companies sponsoring their women leaders. Chief is a membership-and-community company rather than an API provider, so this profile is an identity record in the API Evangelist network with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Cleverdeck
providers.description: CleverDeck is a spaced-repetition flashcard application for iOS, built by an independent developer to help people learn and retain vocabulary and other material more efficiently. It ships hand-made premium decks covering roughly the 3,000 most common words in major foreign languages — Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Russian and advanced English — with translations, transliterations, images, native-speaker audio, and example sentences in both English and the target language. The app uses the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm (as popularized by SuperMemo and Anki) with a customizable learning schedule, cross-device sync, and full offline support. It is free to create and study your own content, with unlimited access to the premium decks for $3 per month. CleverDeck is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or agent-facing surface.

providers.name: Aprende
providers.description: Aprende (Aprende Institute) is an online vocational education platform delivering Spanish-language courses and diplomados to Hispanic entrepreneurs and professionals across the United States and Latin America. The platform offers on-demand, mobile-friendly training across six main areas — gastronomy, entrepreneurship, wellness, beauty, skilled trades, and hospitality/events — taught by expert instructors, and is backed by 500 Global. It operates as a consumer education company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Freckle Education
providers.description: Freckle is an adaptive learning platform from Renaissance that delivers differentiated, standards-aligned math and English Language Arts (ELA) practice for K-12 students. Teachers assign work and monitor progress while students practice at their own level, with the platform adapting question difficulty to each learner across 70,000+ math questions and 1,000+ ELA passages. Administrators manage rosters and dashboards at the school and district level. Freckle is a school- and classroom-facing application acquired by Renaissance Learning; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Mind Candy, Moshi
providers.description: Mind Candy Ltd is a London-based children's media and technology company, originally known for the Moshi Monsters online game and now operating Moshi, an award-winning children's app for sleep, relaxation and learning. Moshi offers hundreds of hours of bedtime stories, sleep sounds, music, white noise and educational activities delivered through iOS and Android consumer apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Moshi is a direct-to-consumer subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Outschool
providers.description: Outschool is an education-technology marketplace for live, small-group online classes for learners ages 3-18. It connects families and independent teachers across 140,000+ subjects — from math and coding to art, music, and hobbies — offered as one-time sessions, ongoing courses, camps, and social clubs delivered over live video. Outschool also serves schools and districts through its for-organizations program. Backed by Bond Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures, and Y Combinator, the platform is a consumer web application; it exposes no publicly documented developer API. The site is powered by an internal, undocumented GraphQL endpoint (outschool.com/graphql) used only by its own front end and largely blocked to crawlers. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record enriched from the provider's public web surface.

providers.name: Parallel Learning
providers.description: Parallel Learning is a special education services and staffing platform that connects K-12 schools and districts with a nationwide network of licensed clinicians for the remote delivery of specialized student support. Through its proprietary, HIPAA/FERPA-compliant Pathway platform it delivers virtual psychoeducational and neurodevelopmental assessments, speech-language therapy, behavioral and mental-health counseling, specialized instruction in reading, writing, and math, and executive-function coaching, pairing secure teletherapy with progress tracking and clinical oversight so districts can meet compliance requirements and improve student outcomes. The company serves thousands of students across dozens of states and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Think Parametric
providers.description: Think Parametric is an online learning platform for architecture, engineering, and design professionals, offering expert-led courses and professional certifications in computational and parametric design tools including Rhino, Grasshopper, Revit, Dynamo, SketchUp, and V-Ray. Membership plans give individuals and organizations access to a library of 60+ courses taught by practitioners from leading firms such as SOM, BIG, Gensler, AECOM, and Arup, alongside community forums, downloadable assets, and progress tracking. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: General Fusion
providers.description: General Fusion is a Canadian fusion energy company founded in 2002 by physicist Dr. Michel Laberge and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia, in the Vancouver area. It is developing Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF), an approach that combines plasma formation, mechanical compression by a liquid metal liner, and practical heat capture for electricity generation. The company operates LM26, which it describes as the world's largest and most powerful operational fusion plasma injector, and reports 24 plasma prototypes, more than 200,000 plasma experiments, 35+ peer-reviewed papers, and roughly 210 issued and pending patents. In July 2026 General Fusion completed a business combination with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III and became the first publicly listed fusion energy company, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker GFUZ. It is an energy hardware and research company rather than a software or API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts. Its only machine-readable public surfaces are a Yoast-generated llms.txt and the WordPress REST discovery index behind its marketing site.

providers.name: Health Scholars
providers.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Hiphen Plant
providers.description: Hiphen Plant provides advanced image analytics solutions for agricultural research. As plant scientists, they build tools that revolutionize how plants can be assessed, bringing the power of image analytics to agricultural research programs for decision-making on genetics, chemistry, and practices.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: Brilliant
providers.description: Brilliant is an online learning platform for interactive STEM education, covering mathematics, computer science, data, and science. Headquartered in San Francisco and used by over ten million learners worldwide, Brilliant pairs guided, problem-first lessons with adaptive practice that blends classic intelligent tutoring systems, machine-learning recommender systems, and natural-language conversations. The platform is delivered through brilliant.org and native iOS and Android apps, with a freemium model and a Brilliant Premium subscription that unlocks the full course catalog, including expanding AI-powered features such as personalized tutoring conversations and on-the-fly generation of interactive content. Brilliant operates as a direct-to-consumer subscription business with an educator program for classroom access; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program, and the `github.com/brilliant` org on GitHub is an unrelated namespace of personal projects rather than an official Brilliant presence.

providers.name: Draxon
providers.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Holberton School
providers.description: Holberton School is a Silicon Valley-born technology education company that trains software and AI engineers through project-based, peer-driven learning rather than traditional lectures. Students build real applications from day one, using AI as a learning partner while developing the collaboration and problem-solving skills employers need, and the school reports a 92% employment rate among alumni. Holberton operates campuses and partner programs globally and delivers curriculum in software engineering, AI/machine learning, cybersecurity, and cloud. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech; the school publishes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Meadow
providers.description: Meadow is a financial technology company delivering modern student financial services to colleges and universities. Its platform spans the full student financial lifecycle — Meadow Price (a mobile, SAI-compliant net price calculator), Meadow Pay (student billing and payments with automated workflows), Meadow Pre (pre-collections for recovering unpaid tuition), and Meadow Checkout (campus-wide collection of non-tuition fees). Meadow helps institutions improve enrollment, retention, and payment outcomes from application through graduation. Backed by Matrix Partners and Y Combinator. No public API or developer platform is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Diraq
providers.description: Diraq is a quantum computing company headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with offices in Palo Alto, California and Boston, Massachusetts. Spun out of UNSW Sydney in 2022 by Professor Andrew Dzurak, Diraq builds quantum processors from silicon spin qubits — quantum information encoded in the spin of single electrons held in quantum dots formed inside structures derived from conventional CMOS transistors, so the qubits can be fabricated on standard semiconductor foundry lines. The company works with imec, NVIDIA and Quantum Machines, has advanced through DARPA's utility-scale quantum computing initiative, and targets a first commercial processor toward the end of the decade. Diraq is a pre-commercial hardware and research organization: as of this profile it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its stated commercial pathway — cloud access to its processors — is still on the roadmap rather than in market.

providers.name: Unacademy
providers.description: Unacademy is a Bangalore-based online learning platform — one of India's largest — offering live classes, courses, study material, and test preparation for competitive exams including UPSC Civil Services, IIT JEE, NEET-UG, SSC, CA Foundation, and CSIR UGC NET, delivered through its web platform and dedicated learner, educator, and parent mobile apps. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Unacademy runs a consumer platform on an internal API (api.unacademy.com) but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: HumanQ
providers.description: HumanQ is an execution-capability and intelligence platform that helps organizations move critical work forward through structured, live execution sprints called QPods. Each QPod is a 60-minute facilitated session, led by trained "Catalysts," for small groups of up to six participants working through decision drag, unclear ownership, and cross-team stalls. HumanQ is offered as HumanQ Scale (an enterprise-wide program with weekly and monthly tracks, on-demand drop-ins, and deep customization) and HumanQ Teams (a manager-led tool for up to four groups, live in two weeks with no contract). Progress is tracked through the QStart, QImpact, and QSignal measurement framework, with delivery across 74 countries. HumanQ is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. It is a managed-services platform and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Sakana AI
providers.description: Sakana AI is a Tokyo-based AI R&D company founded by ex-Google researchers focused on collective intelligence, evolutionary optimization, and nature-inspired AI methods. The company's first commercial product is Sakana Fugu - a multi-agent orchestration system with an OpenAI-compatible API (currently in beta). Sakana also publishes Sakana Chat (consumer) and Sakana Marlin (beta).

providers.name: Peel Therapeutics
providers.description: Peel Therapeutics is an evolutionary-medicine biotechnology company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with research teams in the United States and Israel. Co-founded in 2015 by pediatric oncologist Dr. Joshua Schiffman, the company translates molecules that evolution has already validated in nature into therapeutics for patients with cancer and inflammatory disease. Its founding program is built on elephant p53 (EP53) — elephants carry roughly forty copies of the p53 tumor-suppressor gene against the human two — delivered as liposomal protein nanoparticles, alongside PEEL-224, a TOP1 inhibitor in clinical development. Discovery runs on the company's proprietary, internal Darwin.AI platform and the Darwin Biobank, a comparative-oncology sample collection. Peel is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Web3 Foundation
providers.description: Web3 Foundation is a Swiss nonprofit founded in 2017 by Gavin Wood that funds research and development teams building the foundation of a decentralized web (Web3). It stewards and supports the Polkadot and Kusama networks, operates a research hub and an education/wiki program, and historically ran the Web3 Foundation Grants Program (now discontinued) to seed open-source software and protocol research. It is a funding and research organization rather than a traditional API provider: it publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface, but does maintain an RFC 9116 security.txt and a coordinated vulnerability-disclosure program.

providers.name: Herb
providers.description: Herb (herb.co) is a leading digital media and e-commerce platform dedicated to cannabis culture, education, and lifestyle. It publishes cannabis news, strain databases, product reviews, dispensary and brand guides, deals, recipes, and city-level legalization guides, and operates the "Herb Agency" offering branding and marketing services to cannabis companies. The consumer site is built on Gatsby (React) with a GraphQL data layer, Algolia search, and a Firebase/serverless backend hosted on Netlify. Herb is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio; the company exposes no public developer API program at this time, so this profile captures its published web, content, and discovery surface (llms.txt, domain security posture, and identity/link properties) rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: La Solive
providers.description: La Solive is a French vocational training organization (organisme de formation) preparing career-changers and apprentices for the trades behind building energy renovation and the climate transition. It runs state-recognized, practice-based programs — chef de projet en rénovation énergétique, conducteur de travaux, plombier chauffagiste pompe à chaleur et gaz, technicien de maintenance CVC, installateur de panneaux photovoltaïques, QualiPAC and agent de maintenance du bâtiment — delivered across campuses in Paris, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Toulouse and Lille plus a distance-learning track, with Qualiopi certification and France Travail / Mon Compte Formation / Transitions Pro financing. La Solive reports 1,500+ students trained and 500+ recruiting partner companies. It is a Partech portfolio company in the Climate sector. As of this enrichment pass La Solive publishes no public API, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it does publish an /llms.txt agent-readable site index, captured in this repo.

providers.name: Medley
providers.description: Medley is a leadership development company that delivers group-based executive coaching at enterprise scale, pairing professional coaches with AI-enabled tooling to bring quality and a human touch to Fortune 500 organizations. Founded in 2020 by Edith Cooper and Jordan Taylor, the platform runs curated small-group coaching cohorts focused on trust, empathy, communication, and collaboration to drive organizational transformation. Medley raised a $3.7M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It operates as a B2B services and coaching platform and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Oboe
providers.description: Oboe is an AI-powered learning platform whose mission is to teach one billion people one trillion things. Positioned as "AI that won't make you stupid," it lets anyone learn virtually any subject through a conversational interface that generates personalized, on-demand courses and lessons ("magical courses made just for you"). Founded in New York and backed by Homebrew, Oboe is building what it calls the world's first completely generalized AI-powered learning platform, focused on making humans smarter rather than only making machines smarter. As a consumer web application, Oboe does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; api.oboe.com serves only an XML sitemap index for public course pages.

providers.name: Poker Skill
providers.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Brite
providers.description: Brite is a white-label learning management system (LMS) platform for STEM education, giving educators, academies, and learning centers a single operational tool to run computer-science programs in game and web development. It bundles a ready-made curriculum, classroom and roster management, student progress reporting, and teacher accounts, replacing spreadsheets and disparate software with one branded platform. Brite is offered on free, per-student Professional, and custom school/district tiers. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
providers.description: Since 1958, DARPA has held to an enduring mission: to create technological surprise for U.S. national security. Working with innovators inside and outside government, DARPA invests in transformational breakthroughs across biological technologies, defense sciences, information innovation, microsystems, strategic technology, and tactical technology. DARPA does not expose public developer APIs but does publish an RSS news feed and program information through its website.

providers.name: 1QBit
providers.description: 1QB Information Technologies Inc. (1QBit) is a quantum computing software company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It builds hardware-agnostic algorithms and software for optimization, simulation, and machine learning that run across quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical high-performance computing hardware, with work spanning computational finance, life sciences and quantum chemistry, materials, and telecommunications. 1QBit has hardware and platform partnerships with D-Wave, Fujitsu, IBM, and Microsoft Azure Quantum, and participates in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) on automated design tools for utility-scale quantum computation. The company markets a 1Qloud optimization platform whose own marketing page cites Python SDK, gRPC, and REST API interfaces, but as of August 2026 1QBit publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract — the former portal.1qbit.com host no longer resolves and access is arranged through industry partnerships. Its only public developer surface is a small GitHub organization of research code plus two first-party Python libraries on PyPI.

providers.name: EdSights
providers.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

providers.name: Educ-up
providers.description: Educ-up is a French social-impact education group founded in 2016 by Mohamed El Mazzouji, headquartered in Saint-Denis, La Réunion with establishments in metropolitan France including Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis). It operates two consumer- and professional-facing brands rather than a software product: Domissori, launched in 2019, which places Montessori-trained educators in family homes for childcare, educational workshops and academic tutoring across Vannes, Chambéry, Lyon, Grenoble, Perpignan, Montpellier, Marseille and Saint-Denis; and Edacademy, a Qualiopi-certified training and apprenticeship centre for early-childhood and personal-care professions (CAP AEPE, Titre Pro ADVF, Bac Pro ASSP, parenting and Montessori support). The group also runs Ed'solidaire, a subsidy scheme that opens paid childcare to low-income families. Investors include Serena, M Capital, Inco Ventures, MakeSense and Racine2. Edacademy delivers its programmes through a self-hosted Moodle learning platform at formation.edacademy.fr, but that is an end-user LMS: as of August 2026 Educ-up publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its corporate domain educ-up.fr now redirects to a parked IONOS default site.

providers.name: Kilsar
providers.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: mPower Social
providers.description: mPower Social Enterprises Ltd. is a Dhaka, Bangladesh technology-for-development company founded in 2008 by Harvard and MIT graduate students as ClickDiagnostics — winner of the MIT $100K competition — and renamed after moving its center of gravity to Bangladesh in 2010. mPower designs, builds and operates information systems for governments, UN agencies, donor organizations and international NGOs across health and nutrition, water and sanitation, agriculture and livestock, education, governance and rights, livelihood and poverty alleviation, climate and environment, and humanitarian response, and states it has deployed more than 300 ICT solutions across 17 countries in the Global South. Its engineering practice is built on open-source digital public goods — DHIS2, OpenMRS, OpenSRP / FHIR Core, Bahmni and Moodle — which it customizes, integrates and supports for national health management information systems, electronic medical records and shared health records, rather than shipping a hosted product of its own. The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified. mPower publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; its public software surface is a GitHub organization made up largely of downstream forks of the open-source health platforms it implements, plus a set of first-party Android apps on Google Play.

providers.name: Photonic
providers.description: Photonic Inc. is a Vancouver, British Columbia deep-tech company founded in 2016 by Dr. Stephanie Simmons and led by CEO Dr. Paul Terry, building distributed, fault-tolerant quantum computing and quantum networking on silicon T centre spin-photon qubits. Its "Entanglement First" architecture couples qubits that compute, store and emit telecom-band photons natively, so individual modules can be entangled over ordinary telecom fibre rather than scaled inside a single dilution refrigerator, and its SHYPS QLDPC error-correction codes cut the physical-qubit overhead of fault tolerance. Backed by Microsoft, British Columbia Investment Management Corp, RBC and TELUS, selected for Stage B of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, and intending to deliver quantum computing through Azure and private systems. As of this profile Photonic is pre-commercial from an integration standpoint: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Simbel
providers.description: Simbel is a Paris-based HR technology company (founded 2021, backed by Speedinvest) offering a smart, unified training management suite that combines a Training Management System (TMS) and a Learning Management System (LMS) in one platform. It helps HR and L&D teams automate the full training lifecycle, from need assessment and request approvals through session organization, e-learning delivery, real-time reporting, and legal compliance (BPF, Qualiopi, BDES). Simbel connects to major HRIS and learning tools such as Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, ADP, Lucca, Payfit, BambooHR, 360Learning, and Docebo through pre-built integrations. As of this enrichment pass Simbel publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal; integrations are delivered as managed connectors rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: FundMiner
providers.description: FundMiner is a fund management and donor stewardship platform for mission-driven organizations, giving universities, healthcare systems, and community foundations one place to manage the full fund lifecycle. It combines fund management with compliance monitoring, impact and donor reporting, and a branded donor portal that gives donors real-time visibility into how their gifts are used. The platform integrates with existing financial systems and offers role-based dashboards and access controls. FundMiner is a Techstars-backed company; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API reference at this time, so this profile captures its public identity and web presence.

providers.name: Guild
providers.description: Guild (formerly Guild Education) is an education benefits and career opportunity platform that partners with large employers to fund and administer workforce education, upskilling, and career-mobility programs for their frontline and hourly employees. Employers offer Guild as a benefit; employees access a curated marketplace of degrees, certificates, bootcamps, English-language, and professional-skilling programs from vetted learning providers, plus coaching and career navigation to move into higher-demand roles. Guild is a B2B/B2B2C SaaS platform sold to enterprise HR and talent-development teams to fill critical roles, improve retention, increase internal mobility, and prove measurable ROI. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado, Guild is a venture-backed company. This profile was surfaced from investor portfolios and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Guild publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Kotcha
providers.description: Kotcha is a consumer running-coaching mobile application operated by PACEUP SAS, a French company based in Paris, and co-founded with marathon world-record holder Eliud Kipchoge and the NN Running Team. The app generates personalized, adaptive training plans for 5K, 10K, half-marathon and marathon distances, delivered through a conversational AI coach that adapts to completed workouts, and it imports activity and health data from Strava, Garmin Connect, Apple, Coros and Huawei wearables. Kotcha raised EUR 3.5M in October 2025 in a round led by Racine2, operated by Serena and makesense. Kotcha is a consumer subscription product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its terms of service explicitly prohibit automated access to the service. This profile records that absence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: OnMyGrad
providers.description: OnMyGrad is a Hong Kong-based campus-recruitment and career-learning SaaS platform that helps employers connect with university talent across Southeast Asia through virtual job-tasting and work-experience programs. Founded in 2021 by Jesse Chow and Chun Hin Anthony So, its B2B2C "OnMyGrad Space" lets employers build branded profiles, run virtual talent pipelines, and evaluate candidates, while students access immersive career and industry learning content from leading employers. The company launched its MVP in February 2021, raised pre-seed funding from 500 Global, and is expanding into Singapore and Taiwan. It operates a public marketing site and a web application but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Prisms VR
providers.description: Prisms VR (Prisms) is an educational technology company building what it calls the world's first spatial learning platform, where students learn core math, science, and other subjects by abstracting up from immersive, first-person physical experiences delivered in virtual reality. Founded by MIT engineer-turned-educator Anurupa Ganguly, the teacher-facing platform uses kinesthetic, embodied learning to help students grasp abstract concepts and aims to develop curious, resilient thinkers. Prisms is an a16z portfolio company; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and profiled through the enrichment pipeline. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Quero Educação
providers.description: Quero Educação is a Brazilian education-technology company that operates a marketplace connecting students with higher-education institutions across Brazil. Its flagship product Quero Bolsa lets students compare colleges, courses and schools with price transparency and enroll online at discounted tuition, while a suite of institution-facing products — Nota Quero (online entrance exams), Matrícula Digital (digital enrollment), Quero Pago (tuition payments) and Quero Analytics (data intelligence) — helps partner schools fill seats and manage admissions. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It maintains a private GitHub organization and a public engineering blog on Medium, but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or published API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public identity, domain-security posture, and commercial/legal surfaces.

providers.name: CodeMentor
providers.description: CodeMentor (codementor.io) is an on-demand marketplace that connects software developers with vetted expert mentors for live 1:1 coding help, code review, debugging, pair programming, and longer-term freelance engagements across dozens of programming languages and frameworks. Part of the Arc / CodeMentor group, it serves individual learners seeking real-time mentorship as well as companies hiring vetted remote developers. As of this profile CodeMentor exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this record was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with verified identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Four Pillars
providers.description: Four Pillars is a research-driven blockchain enterprise headquartered in Asia, operating through three divisions: FP Research publishes primary analysis of crypto protocols, markets, and policy with deep regional expertise across Korea and the broader Asian market; FP Validated runs validator and node infrastructure across proof-of-stake networks, pairing research with live operations; and FP Institution advises banks, financial institutions, and corporates on blockchain strategy. The firm serves founders, funds, and regulators, and is a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. It is a research and advisory business rather than a developer-facing API platform, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Quantum Circuits
providers.description: Quantum Circuits, Inc. is a quantum computing hardware company (a Yale University spinout) building superconducting quantum systems with built-in error detection. Its dual-rail cavity qubits pair Quantum Error Detection (QED), Real-Time Control Flow (RTCF), and Error Detection Handling (EDH), and its Aqumen Seeker QPU (introduced November 2024) targets stable, repeatable, fault-tolerant quantum computation. The company engages early users through a Strategic Quantum Release (SQR) program that includes a simulator and access to Aqumen Seeker systems, rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ring Therapeutics
providers.description: Ring Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering that develops targeted vector conjugate medicines built on the human commensal virome. Its Anellogy platform harnesses anelloviruses — commensal viruses that co-exist with the human immune system — to generate gene delivery vectors with tissue-specific tropism and the potential to be redosed. Ring has sequenced thousands of anelloviruses into what it describes as the largest anellovirus database assembled to date, and has raised more than $250 million across Series A, B and C financings. The company is a therapeutics developer rather than a software provider: it publishes a corporate site, a press release stream and a scientific publications list, and operates no public API, developer portal or SDK.

providers.name: Cvent Community
providers.description: Cvent Community is Cvent's customer support, knowledge base, certification, and peer-to-peer forum hub at community.cvent.com. It is the 24/7 destination where event professionals learn Cvent products, search the Knowledge Base, take Cvent Academy training and certification courses, and exchange best practices with other users through Open Forum and product-specific learning centers (Attendee Hub, Registration, OnArrival, Surveys, Cvent Supplier Network, Event Diagramming, Cvent Studio, Cvent Webinar, Passkey). Cvent Community is not itself an API product; programmatic access to Cvent data is delivered via the Cvent Platform REST API at api-platform.cvent.com using OAuth 2.0 client credentials.

providers.name: Daybreak
providers.description: Daybreak Health is a B2B mental health company that delivers teletherapy and mental health programs for K-12 students (ages 5-19) in partnership with school districts and health plans. Its services include one-on-one teletherapy, in-person and hybrid onsite programs, universal mental health screeners, and mental health classes, with programs tailored for BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and low-income student populations. Daybreak is a care-delivery organization sold to schools and payers rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer or API surface. This APIs.json profile captures the company's public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Experiment
providers.description: Experiment is an online crowdfunding platform for scientific research that connects scientists directly with backers who fund individual studies. Researchers across biology, chemistry, medicine, physics, computer science, paleontology, economics, engineering, and neuroscience post projects with goals and budgets; the public pledges funds, follows lab notes, and shares in the discoveries. Experiment (formerly Microryza) also supports university institutions and dedicated funding programs, and publishes results and updates back to funders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, slow-ventures, and y-combinator and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a live consumer website but no public developer API, docs, or well-known surface.

providers.name: Future
providers.description: Future (Future Research, Inc., future.co) is a consumer fitness technology company that delivers custom, one-on-one personal training through a mobile app. Members are paired with a dedicated certified coach who builds an individualized workout program, provides real-time messaging and accountability check-ins, and adapts the plan over time. The product includes an exercise library with form-guidance videos, flexible scheduling, and Apple Watch integration for workout tracking. Future is a direct-to-consumer subscription service (first month $50, then $199/month with a 30-day money-back guarantee) and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company.

providers.name: Antimatter Systems
providers.description: Antimatter Systems is an education technology company building a peer-to-peer learning network where students demonstrate mastery by making memes, puzzles, and games rather than by writing essays or sitting tests. Founded by Jonathan Libov, the company raised a $2M seed round led by Version One Ventures in 2023, joined by Spacecadet, Ordinary Holdings, Haystack and Compound. Its classroom product lets teachers create meme-based activities with deadlines and instructions, invite students by shareable link, moderate submissions, restrict learners to view-only, work from a library of pre-approved templates, catch unedited-image uploads with plagiarism detection, and grade every submission in one place; the company states it should be free for schools. Antimatter also ships a Sorcerer AI instructional coach plus the consumer Antimatter: Creator and Antimatter: Universe iOS apps. The platform runs on the web at playantimatter.com. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Arivihan
providers.description: Arivihan is an Indian EdTech company operating an AI-based, fully automated online learning platform that gives each K-12 school student a personalized "tutor in their pocket." It targets low- and middle-income families and students in Tier 2+ cities, delivering interactive, personalized lectures and doubt resolution in vernacular languages at roughly 10% of typical coaching fees. Products include the DoubtBuzzter mobile app and the tutor-prod / InstantGuru doubt-resolution web platform. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and prosus-ventures. No public API or developer surface was found during enrichment; this remains a consumer-facing product profile.

providers.name: Descomplica
providers.description: Descomplica is a Brazilian online education (edtech) company founded in 2011 and headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, offering a digital learning platform for ENEM and vestibular exam prep, K-12 (Escolar), undergraduate and graduate (Pós-graduação) degrees, public-exam (Concursos) preparation, and corporate training. The platform delivers live and recorded classes, study plans, tutoring, exercises, and support materials to millions of Brazilian students, and is MEC-authorized. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company operates consumer and corporate learning products but does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: Dreambound
providers.description: Dreambound is a career and technical education marketplace that helps job seekers discover, compare, and enroll in vocational training programs across healthcare, technology, business, and the skilled trades. The platform aggregates thousands of schools and hundreds of programs, letting students filter by location, schedule, format (online, hybrid, or in person), and price, with enrollment coaches guiding them into certifications such as certified nursing assistant, medical billing, phlebotomy, and sterile processing. The service is free for students and monetizes through schools and workforce partners who list and advertise their programs. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Collaborative Fund, and 8VC, Dreambound is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: EDUFI PTE. LTD
providers.description: EduFi (EDUFI PTE. LTD) is a Singapore-incorporated education-financing fintech operating Pakistan's first Study Now, Pay Later (SNPL) digital platform, with expansion into Saudi Arabia and Oman. The Shariah-approved platform lets parents and students finance private schooling, higher education, and international student loans through quick, collateral-free approvals with direct disbursement to educational institutes and convenient monthly installments. EduFi also provides partner educational institutes a free ERP system and subsidized SNPL for their students, and works with financial institutions to fund receivables. Backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist; EduFi publishes a consumer marketing and application surface but no public developer/API program.

providers.name: GoStudent
providers.description: GoStudent is an online tutoring platform headquartered in Vienna, Austria, offering personalized one-on-one lessons across 30+ subjects for K-12 and university students. Founded in 2016, it matches learners with vetted tutors and delivers lessons through its own video-classroom apps for iOS, Android, and web, sold as a monthly subscription. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and Speedinvest, GoStudent grew into one of Europe's largest edtech companies and has acquired peers including Tus Media, Seneca Learning, and Studienkreis. GoStudent does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web properties and domain-security posture as a network lead.

providers.name: Guild Education
providers.description: Guild is an education benefits platform that helps large employers turn workforce education into workforce strategy. Guild connects a company's frontline and hourly workers to a curated marketplace of debt-free education, upskilling, and career-development programs delivered through vetted learning partners (universities, bootcamps, and skilling providers), and pairs that access with coaching and analytics so HR leaders can fill critical roles, improve retention, increase internal mobility, and prove measurable ROI. Guild operates as a B2B2C platform: employers fund and administer the benefit, learning partners supply the programs, and members (employees) enroll and progress toward degrees, certificates, and new durable skills. Guild does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public company and web-property surface.

providers.name: Lovevery
providers.description: Lovevery is a direct-to-consumer children's brand that designs stage-based Play Kits, books, and learning products for infants and toddlers, grounded in child-development research. It operates a Shopify-backed e-commerce and subscription storefront at lovevery.com with a customer help center, blog, and careers site. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network, Lovevery publishes no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mentor Collective
providers.description: Mentor Collective operates an AI Mentorship OS for higher education, powering peer mentoring, student success, and retention programs at colleges and universities. Its platform matches and onboards mentors and mentees, guides conversations with AI prompts, surfaces risk signals and belonging gaps, and turns connection data into real-time retention intelligence for institutions. Backed by Techstars, the company serves higher-education and workforce partners. As of this profile Mentor Collective publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this repo captures its public web, blog, legal, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Peak
providers.description: Peak is a consumer brain-training mobile application operated by Synaptic Labs (formerly Peak Labs) that offers cognitive exercise games and personalized workouts spanning memory, attention, problem-solving, mental agility, language, and emotion. Its games and Advanced Training Programmes are developed with researchers from institutions including Cambridge, Yale, UCL, and King's College London. Peak Pro is a subscription that unlocks 40+ games, personalized workouts, performance analytics, and an AI Coach. Peak is a mobile-only consumer product distributed via the App Store and Google Play and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Praktika.ai Company
providers.description: Praktika.ai is an AI-powered language-learning application that lets learners have spoken conversations with lifelike AI avatar tutors and receive instant feedback on pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary. The product spans mobile (iOS and Android) and web, with personalized study plans and speaking, listening, reading, and writing exercises across many languages, plus a B2B offering for organizations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Praktika publishes a consumer product only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation were found — so this profile captures the company identity and web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Saturn
providers.description: Saturn is a mobile calendar and scheduling app built for high school students, designed around the complexities of the school day, built around your friends, and kept truly real-time. Students import their class schedule, see what their friends are doing, coordinate activities, and share their calendar socially. The company positions itself as "the next generation calendar, enabling time together for all." Saturn is a consumer iOS and Android application distributed through the App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by General Catalyst and Insight Partners, with notable individual investors including Jeff Bezos, Marc Benioff, and Dara Khosrowshahi.

providers.name: Seekho
