The company turns complex human knowledge - tax codes, clinical guidelines, legal rules, and safety constraints - into machine-checkable logic, so that every AI answer can be traced, challenged, and proved rather than merely sounding plausible. Its stack compiles domain rules into formal systems that return proofs, counterexamples, and traceable explanations. Pramaana Labs raised $27M to build a compiler for mission-critical AI and is backed by Accel. At this time the company operates as a research lab with published work (RuleArena, arXiv) and no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Sequence Bio
providers.description: Sequence Bio is a life sciences and population genomics company based in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, focused on discovering the genetic causes of disease to power the development of new medicines. The company leverages the founder-effect genetics of the Newfoundland and Labrador population, running a large-scale Study of the Genetic Causes of Inherited Disease to identify novel drug targets and predictors of treatment response for pharmaceutical partners. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a corporate and research website but does not currently expose a public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pair
providers.description: Pair (formerly Inversity) is an enterprise AI adoption platform that helps organizations build workforce capability in artificial intelligence and measure the return on their AI investment. Pair delivers personalized, hands-on masterclasses grounded in each learner's role, industry, and day-to-day tasks — covering tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude, plus agentic AI — moving teams from basic AI awareness to measurable adoption. A multi-tier certification path (Fundamentals, Proficiency, Mastery), team adoption dashboards, ROI measurement that tracks time saved and business impact, an AI Showcase for sharing effective workflows, and manager oversight tools round out the platform. Pair is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: CEPS (Centre for European Policy Studies)
providers.description: Founded in Brussels in 1983, the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) is a leading independent think tank and forum for debate on EU affairs, with an exceptionally strong in-house research capacity and an extensive network of partner institutes. CEPS conducts rigorous, evidence-based policy research on European and global issues (Data Governance Act, Data Act, AI Act, climate, migration, financial markets) and disseminates its findings primarily through publications, events, and podcasts rather than a commercial API; programmatic access to CEPS output is primarily via public RSS, OPML feeds, and structured publication pages on ceps.eu.

providers.name: Emma
providers.description: Emma (by EDAILABS) is an AI-powered English language learning application built around a 3D interactive avatar tutor that offers real-time spoken conversation practice, instant pronunciation and grammar corrections, and personalized, adaptive learning paths. Positioned as "more than just a chatbot," the app models native accents and speech patterns for judgment-free practice available 24/7, and reports more than 500,000 users. It is a consumer iOS mobile application backed by Seedcamp; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Jade Autism
providers.description: Jade (Jade ND) is a Brazil-, UAE-, and UK-based education technology company building inclusive digital solutions for neurodivergent children, including those on the autism spectrum (ASD). Its product family includes Jade Edu (personalized-learning software for schools and educators), the Jade App (cognitive-development games for children, with 185,000+ downloads across 179 countries), Jade Astea (eye-tracking technology that assists professionals in evaluating autism-spectrum diagnosis), and Jade Academy (professional-development courses on inclusive and diverse education). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tarefa
providers.description: Tarefa (tarefa.co) is an online study companion — "tu compañero de estudio" — for Spanish-speaking university and high-school students, offering structured learning paths, solved exercises ("ejercicios resueltos"), video tutorials, and practice materials across mathematics (calculus, differential equations, probability and statistics, numerical methods), physics (electromagnetism, Newtonian mechanics, energy), and chemistry (inorganic, organic, gas laws, atomic structure, electrochemistry). It is a subscription-based B2C EdTech platform backed by 500 Global. Tarefa exposes no public developer API or documentation at this time; this profile captures its public web surface and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TutorABC
providers.description: TutorABC (formerly iTutorGroup) is a Taiwan-headquartered online language-learning platform offering live one-on-one and small-group English and Chinese instruction to learners worldwide. Courses span conversational and business English, Mandarin Chinese, certification-exam prep, and study-abroad advising, delivered through a proprietary web and mobile classroom with matched tutors and partnerships with institutions such as Oxford and Cambridge. The company runs consumer learning sites alongside separate portals for tutor recruitment, learning consultants, and interviewer/onboarding workflows. TutorABC is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company identity, its agent-facing llms.txt, and its domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Presence
providers.description: Presence is a student engagement and co-curricular involvement platform for higher education, now part of Modern Campus. It helps colleges and universities manage student organizations, campus events, involvement and attendance tracking, co-curricular records, forms, and engagement analytics so institutions can attract, engage, and retain learners. Modern Campus serves more than 1,700 colleges, universities, and education providers. Presence is delivered as a closed SaaS product with support and reference code available through the Modern Campus customer support portal; there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-service API surface published at this time, so this profile captures company identity and probed domain security rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Prodigy Education
providers.description: Prodigy Education is a Canadian K-8 game-based learning company best known for Prodigy Math and Prodigy English — fantasy RPG-style products in which students battle and quest by answering curriculum-aligned questions. The product is free for teachers and is monetized through optional parent memberships. Prodigy is consumer- and classroom-facing with no public developer API or partner program. Its integration surface is school rostering and SSO: Clever (SSO + Secure Sync district rostering), ClassLink (SSO, with OneRoster district rostering rolling out), and Google (SSO + Google Classroom assignment creation).

providers.name: Rebel Girls
providers.description: Rebel Girls is a global media and publishing brand that celebrates inspiring stories about girls and women, empowering young audiences through books, a podcast, a YouTube channel, apparel and accessories, activities, and the Rebel Girls Sport program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Rebel Girls publishes no developer, API, or well-known discovery surface: rebelgirls.com redirects to www.rebelgirls.com and every standard well-known endpoint returns 404, and there are no developer/api subdomains. This profile captures the company's public identity and a live domain-security posture probe; it carries no API artifacts because there is no public API to describe.

providers.name: Endless Studios LLC
providers.description: Endless Studios LLC is a game development learning platform where aspiring creators learn to build video games through real, pro-studio projects. Its Endstar game engine lets creators code and collaborate in real time, while structured programs (Launchpad for beginners, Capstone for advanced participants) pair learners with 30+ game-industry mentors, expert playtesting, and collaborator matching across design, art, and programming. Learners build portfolios of shipped games to show potential employers. The company runs university, government, and partner programs (including a UAE national game-making competition) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment (consumer/creator-facing product on the studio.endlessstudios.com app).

providers.name: Noodle Partners
providers.description: Noodle Partners (Noodle) is a higher education solutions company providing full-funnel services and AI-powered products spanning student recruitment through graduation and workforce development. Its product suite includes the Noodle Learning Platform (a customizable LMS for lifelong learning and continuing education), Noodle Companion (an in-platform AI assistant), Noodle Engage (conversational AI for recruitment and enrollment), Noodle Dialogue (AI-assisted faculty content and curriculum design), and Noodle Manage (data integration and analytics). Noodle also delivers marketing, enrollment, learning design, retention, and strategic consulting services to universities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; the company publishes a SOC 2 trust center.

providers.name: The Cru
providers.description: The Cru (now branded "The Cru Empowered by Luminary") is a membership community founded by Tiffany Dufu that matches women and allies into small peer-coaching accountability circles ("Crus") of 6-8 members who meet in monthly 90-minute gatherings to advance their personal and professional goals. It was acquired by Luminary, a New York City based professional community and coworking organization, and the thecru.com site now redirects to weareluminary.com/luminary-crus. This is a consumer community and coaching business, not a technical platform - it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Revolution Foods
providers.description: Revolution Foods is an Oakland, California food company founded in 2006 by Kristin Groos Richmond and Kirsten Saenz Tobey that manufactures and delivers nutritious, freshly prepared meals to schools and senior communities. It is the largest K-12 school meal vendor in California, serving more than 35 million meals a year across 800+ schools and senior centers, with programs spanning district and charter school food service, after-school and summer meals, senior center dining and homebound delivery. The company has been a Certified B Corporation since 2009 and a Public Benefit Corporation since 2021, and reports a 100% audit pass rate across NSLP, SBP, CACFP, SFSP and Title III compliance. Customers order through Centro, a login-gated web ordering portal; Revolution Foods publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Studocu
providers.description: Studocu (operated by StudeerSnel B.V., Amsterdam) is a global online learning platform and study-materials marketplace where students access, share, and upload course documents, lecture notes, summaries, and exam prep across thousands of institutions and subjects. The platform layers AI study tools on top of its crowdsourced document library — an Ask AI chat, AI Notes generation, and an AI Quiz Generator — alongside course organization, study lists, and a Premium subscription for unlimited downloads and full document access. Backed by Partech and Point Nine, Studocu was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public security, trust, and web-property surface.

providers.name: Brightwheel
providers.description: Brightwheel (mybrightwheel.com) is an all-in-one childcare and early education management platform used by childcare centers, preschools, and early-learning programs to run daily operations - attendance and check-in, digital daily sheets, tuition billing and payments, enrollment and admissions, staff/timecards, classroom (room) management, learning assessments, and real-time parent messaging and photo/video sharing. As of this catalog entry, Brightwheel does NOT publish a documented, self-serve public or partner developer API. There is no developer portal, API reference, API key signup, OpenAPI specification, or webhook documentation. The only Brightwheel API activity that is publicly acknowledged is bespoke, contract-scoped work built for individual government partners - for example a private API implemented to submit attendance and subsidy data to Iowa's childcare subsidy data system - and inbound integrations where Brightwheel pushes data into third-party products (e.g. staff timecards to Gusto for payroll). None of these expose a documented API surface that outside developers can build against. This entry is therefore an honest stub documenting the provider and its access model; no API definitions are asserted because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: University of Bologna Open Data
providers.description: University of Bologna Open Data is a university open-data portal for Italy running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 34 datasets.

providers.name: UPM YODA Open Data Portal
providers.description: UPM YODA Open Data Portal is a university open-data portal for Spain running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API over approximately 201 datasets.

providers.name: Junto Education
providers.description: Junto is a Berlin-based leadership-development company and a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. Junto delivers cohort-based, live and interactive online training led by certified coaches who previously held senior leadership roles at leading technology companies. Its programs combine the accountability and personal interaction of offline training with the scalability of online learning, and cover first-time managers, high-performance teams, and custom leadership tracks. Junto sells directly to organizations, who nominate high-potential employees for the programs. Junto operates a marketing site at junto.eu and a customer learning application at app.junto.eu. As of this profile, Junto publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: MasterClass
providers.description: MasterClass is an online education streaming platform where members learn from a roster of 200+ world-renowned instructors across categories including Arts & Entertainment, Business, Design & Style, Sports & Gaming, Writing, Food, Music, Science & Tech, Home & Lifestyle, Community & Government, and Wellness. Content is delivered as video lessons with downloadable workbooks on web, iOS, Android, Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire TV under Standard, Plus, and Premium membership plans. Newer offerings include MasterClass at Work, MasterClass On Call, and the AI-native MasterClass Executive program. Founded by David Rogier; backed by Atomico, Bloomberg Beta, and IVP. MasterClass exposes no public developer API — it is a consumer edtech product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Coded
providers.description: CODED is a Kuwait-based coding education and technology skills company offering hands-on bootcamps and programs for adults, youth, and kids. Its adult bootcamps cover Cybersecurity, Agentic AI, AI & Data Science, and AI App Development, while youth tracks (ages 14-24) and kids programs (ages 6-13) build foundational and career-oriented tech skills through projects, coaching, and real-world standards. CODED also delivers custom enterprise training for corporate teams. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; CODED is an education provider and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or specifications.

providers.name: Collegepulse
providers.description: College Pulse is an American market research and data analytics firm that specializes in survey-based insights from college students. Through an online student panel of 800,000+ verified undergraduates across 1,500+ campuses in all 50 states, it has collected 130+ million survey responses and offers custom research, brand trackers, and syndicated reports to brands, media, and nonprofit organizations. Its work is used by outlets and institutions including The New York Times, the Knight Foundation, FiveThirtyEight, Forbes, Dell, GE, and Chegg. College Pulse is a research services company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public web surface and domain security posture.

providers.name: Disrupt
providers.description: Disrupt Technology Venture is a Bangkok, Thailand-based organization focused on building the country's startup ecosystem and developing future-ready business leaders through education, executive training, and venture investment. Its offerings include the House of Talents (HOT) executive leadership curriculum, the Advanced Executive Program (AXP), corporate in-house training, and the Disrupt MBA online course platform, alongside investment vehicles such as the Disrupt Health Impact Fund (deep-tech healthcare) and the Stormbreaker edtech startup accelerator. Disrupt reports 1,500+ program alumni, 20+ corporate clients (including KBank, PTT, Unilever, and Central Group), and that 7 of the top 10 Thai startups count Disrupt alumni among their founders. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Disrupt publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: MasteryConnect
providers.description: MasteryConnect is a K-12 formative assessment and standards-mastery platform, now part of Instructure. It helps teachers and districts build standards-aligned assessments (from prebuilt items or custom content), deliver common and benchmark assessments, auto-score results, and turn the data into intuitive mastery reports that guide interventions. It integrates tightly with the Canvas LMS through single sign-on and real-time data synchronization. MasteryConnect was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; it was acquired by Instructure in 2019 and does not publish a standalone public developer API — integration is delivered through the Canvas LMS platform and its REST API.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States, operating physical bookstores and an e-commerce site selling books, magazines, gifts, and educational products. Barnes & Noble also operates the Nook e-reader platform and offers affiliate and publisher partner programs. No public developer API is currently offered; the company operates primarily through retail channels and affiliate marketing programs.

providers.name: doubleAI
providers.description: doubleAI (legal entity AAI Technologies Ltd.) is an Israeli AI research company building Artificial Expert Intelligence (AEI) — AI systems that focus their full training capacity on a single technical domain to match and surpass leading human experts, rather than pursuing broad general intelligence. Its flagship system, WarpSpeed, is an AI GPU performance engineer that optimizes NVIDIA kernels, beating hand-tuned expert baselines on the majority of tested kernels. Founded in late 2023 by Prof. Amnon Shashua and Prof. Shai Shalev-Shwartz and based in Ramat Gan, Israel, the company has raised roughly $221M from Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Michael Dell, Bessemer Venture Partners, Pitango First, and Greenfield Partners at a valuation exceeding $1B. doubleAI publishes research and open-source code but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: IMP Software
providers.description: IMP Software builds MAT-first financial management software for the UK education sector. Its flagship product, IMP Planner, is a single-database, trust-wide platform for budgeting, forecasting, reporting, Integrated Curriculum Financial Planning (ICFP) and purchasing, used by Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) and their schools. Based in Exeter, UK, the company is trusted by more than 550 trusts across roughly 6,000 schools and secured a growth investment from Partech in September 2025. IMP Planner is a closed SaaS application for trust finance teams; IMP Software does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers)
providers.description: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) is one of the Big Four professional services firms, with approximately 370,000 staff across a global network of member firms coordinated by PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL). PwC organizes delivery across three primary service lines — Assurance (audit), Tax (tax compliance, planning, and reporting), and Advisory (consulting, deals, and risk). The firm operates proprietary technology platforms including PwC Halo (a suite of data analytics tools used to support audit engagements), the Trusted AI initiative (PwC's responsible-AI governance and assurance framework), and ProEdge (a workforce upskilling platform). In April 2024 PwC announced a multi-year alliance with OpenAI positioning the firm as both OpenAI's largest customer and its first reseller of ChatGPT Enterprise, supporting PwC's broader generative-AI consulting practice. PwC's research and insights surface — pwc.com/insights, the annual Global CEO Survey, the Global Workforce Hopes and Fears Survey, the Money Tree report, and regional industry outlooks — is the firm's primary public-facing knowledge product. PwC does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, partner API documentation, or a GitHub organization at the corporate level. The github.com/pwc handle is held by an unrelated individual user (Patrick Clearwater). Any technical integrations with PwC platforms are arranged through engagement contracts and the PwC Technology Consulting practice rather than through self-service developer credentials. PwC's content distribution is reader-facing (newsletter subscriptions, the PwC US Newsroom, LinkedIn, YouTube) with no documented public RSS feed endpoint exposing news, press releases, or insights as a syndication contract.

providers.name: Echo Labs
providers.description: Echo Labs is a San Francisco-based company building AI-powered media accessibility for higher education. Its platform audits, captions, and audio describes entire institutional video libraries within 24 hours, producing ADA / Title II and WCAG 2.1 AA compliant closed captions and audio descriptions at claimed accuracy above 99 percent and roughly $0.75 per minute — a fraction of legacy vendor pricing. Echo integrates with major learning management systems (7+ LMS platforms) so universities and colleges can bring existing course video into compliance at institutional scale. The company is SOC 2 certified, completed a pre-seed round, and is a Techstars portfolio company. This API Evangelist profile tracks Echo Labs as a company in the network; the provider does not publish a public API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Fidu
providers.description: Fidu is an operating system and financial-services platform for private K-12 schools across Spanish-speaking Latin America. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Fidu digitizes the academic, administrative, financial, and communication processes of educational institutions in a single platform. School administrators send tuition statements and pay slips to families, who then pay tuition directly through the Fidu mobile app, and a "Parent Copilot" AI layer handles 24/7 automated responses, content generation, and academic-data synchronization with school information systems. Fidu raised a $5M seed round led by NFX and Lightspeed Venture Partners and reports more than 1,000 institutions across 10 countries and over 500,000 active users. Fidu does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures the company's real public web properties only.

providers.name: Metafy
providers.description: Metafy is a consumer marketplace for gaming coaching and mentorship, connecting players with expert coaches and professional gamers for personalized one-on-one lessons, VOD reviews, and guides across popular competitive titles. Metafy operates a consumer web platform at metafy.gg and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; the only machine-discoverable surface found was an RFC 9116 /.well-known/security.txt security contact. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures.

providers.name: Myu
providers.description: Myu (MyU Interactive Learning) is an education-technology company offering an integrated learning management system (LMS) and school management platform that unifies class delivery, a student information system (SIS), grading and academic reporting, attendance and compliance tracking, and parent/teacher communication in a single interface. It serves early-childhood centers, K-12 schools, higher-education institutions, training institutes, and individual teachers across 1,000+ institutions worldwide, with a notable presence in the GCC region. Myu is delivered as web and mobile (iOS/Android) applications and, as of this profiling, exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Safe Superintelligence
providers.description: Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) is an AI research lab founded in 2024 by Ilya Sutskever, Daniel Gross, and Daniel Levy, with offices in Palo Alto and Tel Aviv. The company describes safe superintelligence as its single mission, sole focus, and "entire product roadmap," and is assembling a lean team of engineers and researchers dedicated to it and nothing else. SSI raised $1B in a Series A from NFDG, a16z, Sequoia, DST Global, and SV Angel; Ilya Sutskever serves as CEO and Daniel Levy as President. The company publishes no public API, developer platform, or technical documentation as of this enrichment pass — this profile captures its identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Humans
providers.description: humans& is a human-centric frontier AI lab founded in 2025 and publicly announced on January 20, 2026, building large-scale AI models centered on people and their relationships rather than raw autonomy. Its research spans long-horizon and multi-agent reinforcement learning, memory, and user understanding, tightly integrating science and product so that AI acts as connective tissue that strengthens organizations and communities. The founding team comes from frontier industry and academic labs including xAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Meta, Reflection, AI2, Stanford, and MIT. Its seed round is led by SV Angel and co-founder Georges Harik, with investors including NVIDIA, GV (Google Ventures), Emerson Collective, Forerunner, S32, DCVC, and Jeff Bezos. As a pre-product research lab it publishes no public API yet; this profile captures its verified public identity surfaces.

providers.name: Magoosh
providers.description: Magoosh is an online test-preparation company serving over 10 million students across 185 countries with affordable, self-paced courses for the GRE, GMAT, SAT, ACT, TOEFL, IELTS, MCAT, and LSAT. Its platform pairs expert-crafted practice questions, video lessons, and detailed explanations with progress tracking, flashcard tools, AI-assisted tutoring, and iOS/Android apps, plus school and district plans. Magoosh publishes a marketing website and a company blog but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web footprint and domain security posture.

providers.name: Swiss Education Group
providers.description: Swiss Education Group (SEG) is a Montreux-based alliance of internationally celebrated hospitality, business, and culinary arts schools in Switzerland, comprising Cesar Ritz Colleges, Culinary Arts Academy Switzerland, Swiss Hotel Management School, and HIM Business School. Across five campuses it educates more than 6,000 students from over 110 nationalities in hospitality management, culinary arts, and business. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass SEG publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this profile is maintained as a company/identity record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Iris.ai
providers.description: Iris.ai is a Norwegian AI company providing an AI knowledge foundation for regulated enterprises, turning complex enterprise and scientific data into trustworthy, compliant AI. Its platform spans three products — Axion (data organization for AI-ready intelligence), Neuralith (enterprise knowledge integration into AI engines), and RSpace, the Researcher Workspace that lets R&D teams, librarians, and academics search, filter, analyze, extract, summarize, and report across scientific literature. Iris.ai is backed by 500 Global. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: Miruvor AI Inc.
providers.description: Miruvor AI Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech AI research lab building brain-inspired continual learning models. Rather than scaling frozen, pre-trained models, Miruvor uses spiking neural networks as its representational substrate together with local learning rules to build systems that learn from experience in real time, with persistent memory and low-energy, neuromorphic efficiency. Founded out of The Residency and backed by 500 Global, the company is pre-product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Deutscher Wetterdienst
providers.description: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) is Germany's national meteorological service, a federal agency under the Ministry for Digital and Transport, responsible for weather and climate services, warnings, and the national climate archive. Its geospatial surface is an OGC-standard GeoServer at maps.dwd.de serving forecast, radar, warning and climate layers to any WMS or WFS client without a key.

providers.name: Eurac Research
providers.description: Eurac Research is a private research centre in Bolzano, Italy, working across alpine environment, earth observation, health and autonomy studies. Its MAPS portal publishes research datasets — snow cover, land use, climate and remote-sensing products for the Alpine region — through an OGC-standard GeoServer callable anonymously by any GIS client.

providers.name: Flanders Marine Institute
providers.description: The Flanders Marine Institute (Vlaams Instituut voor de Zee, VLIZ) is the Belgian coordination and information platform for marine research, and the operator of Marine Regions, the World Register of Marine Species gazetteer infrastructure and the EMODnet data portals. Its geospatial estate is one of the largest openly callable marine OGC surfaces in Europe.

providers.name: Spacebel s.a.
providers.description: Spacebel s.a. is a Belgian software company building flight and ground software for space missions, including on-board software for ESA missions and Earth-observation ground segments, catalogues and data-access services. Its GIS estate serves Sentinel-derived Earth-observation products through OGC-standard web services.

providers.name: Imbue
providers.description: Imbue is a San Francisco AI research lab building agentic foundation models for reasoning and the human tooling around them, with a stated mission of AI that is loyal to its user. The team trains large reasoning models in-house (including a 70B model trained from scratch with open-sourced tooling and evaluation datasets) and publishes research on agent and reasoning architectures, reinforcement learning, data generation, and the scientific theory of deep learning. Imbue ships practical tools that emerge from the research, including Sculptor and mngr for orchestrating parallel coding agents, Bouncer for filtering social feeds, and Blueprint and Vet. There is no public commercial inference API; integration happens through open-sourced repositories, model artifacts on Hugging Face, and research releases.

providers.name: 51Talk
providers.description: 51Talk is an online English-language education platform that connects learners with certified teachers through one-on-one live video lessons. Founded in 2011 and listed on the NYSE, the company operates across 90+ countries with a large base of accredited teachers, delivering a structured curriculum and ready-made teaching materials for both children and adult learners. Following a strategic shift, 51Talk focuses on international markets outside mainland China, including the Philippines and the broader Southeast Asia region, and recruits teachers globally. It is a consumer education company backed by DCM Ventures; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this repo carries only identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: AssetWorks
providers.description: AssetWorks is an enterprise fleet and asset management software company with more than 40 years of history and over 1,000 customers across commercial and private fleets, government and public works, and higher education. Its products include FleetFocus fleet and enterprise asset management (EAM), Active Assets fixed-asset tracking, Recoup Ops surplus management, and Scan and Validate mobile inventory management. AssetWorks sells on-premise and hosted enterprise software to large fleet and facility operators; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve API program. This repo is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Playbook
providers.description: Playbook is a career-growth platform for women that combines expert-led Masterclasses with an engaged professional community, enabling members to keep learning, build skills, and advance into leadership roles. Its tagline "Connect, Learn, Invest" reflects a focus on peer connection, ongoing education, and investing in one's own career. Playbook is backed by 500 Global and Bain Capital Ventures. As of this profile the company operates a consumer marketing and community web experience and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: UberSense
providers.description: UberSense was a Boston, Massachusetts sports-technology startup whose mobile app provided slow-motion video capture and analysis for coaching athletes, from recreational to Olympic and professional levels. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), UberSense was acquired by Hudl in September 2014 and its technology folded into Hudl's sports video analysis products. The ubersense.com website is now defunct (a decommissioned Heroku app) and the company publishes no public API surface.

providers.name: Bio-Rad Laboratories
providers.description: Bio-Rad Laboratories is a global leader in developing and manufacturing a wide range of products for the life science research and clinical diagnostic markets, including instruments, reagents, consumables, software, and services. Founded in 1952, Bio-Rad serves scientists in genomics, proteomics, cell biology, quality control, and clinical diagnostics with products like real-time PCR systems, western blotting instruments, flow cytometers, and digital PCR.

providers.name: Englease Technologies SPV Ltd
providers.description: Englease is an online English language learning platform serving students across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, founded by Omar Shihan and headquartered in Dubai Internet City, UAE. The platform blends live classes running 16 hours a day across all seven days, self-paced on-demand courses, pronunciation and practice tools, and conversation clubs, with proficiency-based learning paths from beginner to advanced and UK-accredited certifications. Englease serves individuals, corporations, schools, and specific industries including hospitality, call centers, retail, banking, and healthcare. Englease Technologies SPV Ltd is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking. The consumer product is delivered through a web/app experience; no public developer API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Springboard
providers.description: Springboard is an online education company offering mentor-led, career-focused bootcamps and courses in software engineering, data science, data analytics, UX/UI design, cybersecurity, and machine learning. Programs pair a structured, self-paced curriculum with 1:1 industry mentorship, career coaching, and a job guarantee on eligible tracks. Springboard was surfaced from a 500 Global portfolio list and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it operates as a consumer/B2B learning platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile carries identity and security-posture signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Generalist AI
providers.description: Generalist AI is a frontier AI research and product company founded in 2024 that is building general intelligence for the physical world. Rather than manufacturing robots, Generalist builds the embodied foundation models — the "brain" — that run across many robot types and hardware configurations, with an emphasis on dexterity and autonomy. Its founding team of researchers, roboticists, and operators comes from Google DeepMind, Boston Dynamics, and OpenAI, with prior work on PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics, Atlas, Spot, and the scaling of large language models. The company's GEN-1 model (April 2026) is described as the first general-purpose model to reach mastery of simple physical tasks, running with full autonomy. Generalist operates from the Bay Area (San Mateo / San Francisco) and Boston, and has raised more than $500M — including a $400M round at a roughly $2B valuation backed by Nvidia, Bezos Expeditions, Radical Ventures, 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, Hanabi Capital, and boldstart ventures. Generalist AI currently publishes no public API or developer program; this profile captures its company identity and web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Odyssey Ai
providers.description: Odyssey is an AI research lab building general-purpose world models — causal, multimodal systems that understand and simulate physical environments, generating long-form interactive video simulations from text or image prompts rather than text. Its research includes Odyssey-2 (a flagship world model producing multi-minute interactive simulations), Starchild-1 (a real-time multimodal world model), Agora-1 (a multi-agent world simulator), and PROWL-1 (a reinforcement-learning framework for adversarial environment exploration). Odyssey positions world models as foundational AI for robotics, gaming, healthcare, education, and 3D visual asset generation, and raised a $310M Series B. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC. At the time of this profile Odyssey publishes research, writing, and interactive demos but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Parasma
providers.description: Parasma is a San Francisco based biological compute startup building algorithms and hardware that train living human brain cells (cortical neurons on a chip) to perform computation for AI workloads. Founded in 2026 by Sean Cole and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch), the company grew out of research that taught a clump of lab-grown human neurons to play Doom, coverage of which appeared in Nature, The Economist, Scientific American, The Guardian and elsewhere. Parasma currently operates as an early-stage research company with a marketing and news website; it does not yet publish a public API, SDK, developer portal, or other machine-readable developer surface. This profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead so any future developer platform can be captured when it ships.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble Education
providers.description: Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE: BNED) is one of the largest operators of college bookstores in the United States, operating physical and virtual campus stores alongside digital course-materials and educational services. BNED reaches more than 5.7 million students through 1,125+ physical and virtual stores across higher education and K-12 institutions, primarily through its Barnes & Noble College Booksellers subsidiary and the MBS Textbook Exchange wholesale business. Flagship offerings include the First Day and First Day Complete affordable-access course-materials programs, BNC OER+ digital courseware, faculty adoption tools, campus retail and ecommerce services, and BNC AI Tools. BNED separated from Barnes & Noble, Inc. in August 2015 and is not affiliated with the Barnes & Noble retail bookstore chain. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts associated with BNED. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; integrations with campus systems and learning-management systems are delivered through institutional partnerships rather than a public API surface.

providers.name: Ten63 Therapeutics
providers.description: Ten63 Therapeutics is an AI-driven drug-discovery company spun out of Duke University in 2019 and operating from San Francisco, Durham and Boston. It builds BEYOND, which the company describes as the world's first Large Quantum Chemistry Model — pairing generative chemistry at scale (Move37) with a quantum-accurate forcefield and molecular-dynamics engine (Astrolabe) in an approach it calls Superlearning. BEYOND is used to design therapeutics for previously undruggable and under-drugged targets, with an internal pipeline focused on oncology and platform partnerships such as the multi-target collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim. Ten63 is a therapeutics company, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. It does publish an llms.txt describing the company and platform for AI agents.

providers.name: Altera
providers.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

providers.name: Elorian AI
providers.description: Elorian AI Inc is a Palo Alto, California frontier AI research company founded in 2025 and emerged from stealth in April 2026, building foundation models for visual reasoning — models that process visual input directly rather than first converting imagery into text, with the stated goal of advancing toward "visual AGI" for applications in architecture, automotive, manufacturing and robotics. It was co-founded by Andrew Dai (CEO, formerly Google Brain and DeepMind, first author of the 2015 work introducing LM pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, co-lead of GLaM and PaLM 2 pretraining), Yinfei Yang (Chief Multimodal Architect, formerly Apple Foundation Model Multimodal and co-creator of ALIGN at Google Research) and Seth Neel (formerly a Harvard professor researching data-centric generative AI), with Dustin Tran (formerly xAI post-training lead) as Chief Reasoning Architect. The company raised a $55M seed round at a reported $300M valuation with Nvidia and Menlo Ventures as strategic partners, and was named to the Forbes Next Billion-Dollar Startups 2026 list. As of this profiling pass Elorian is pre-product: its site states the first foundation visual thinking model will be released "later this year" and offers only an early-access waitlist. It publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification, and no public API host.

providers.name: Experiential Labs
providers.description: Experiential Labs is an applied AI research laboratory (Y Combinator Summer 2026, San Francisco) building world models that let AI agents simulate reality with high fidelity. Founded by Kion Fallah (former staff research scientist at Waabi) and Silen Naihin (AutoGPT and agent-benchmark contributor, co-founder of Stackwise), the company adapts techniques from autonomous-vehicle development to reconstruct environments at high accuracy and pursue recursive self-improvement and continual learning across domains. Its public work is open source on GitHub, including the world-model-harness (world-model-as-a-harness for simulating AI agent environments), OpenCLaaS (Continual Learning as a Service), and autoresearch-distillation. The company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Lego
providers.description: The LEGO Group is a Danish toy company and the world's largest manufacturer of interlocking plastic building bricks. The company extends its brand across video games, theme parks, movies, educational products, and licensed sets for children and adults. LEGO does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; consumer-facing systems and partner integrations are closed. A public GitHub organization hosts internal engineering tooling and open-source contributions.

providers.name: Philon
providers.description: Philon is a Y Combinator-backed robotics research company building open-source, general-purpose humanoid robots capable of performing unsafe, repetitive, or boring tasks. Philon develops foundational AI models for embodied agents, including Holo 1.0, a generalist vision-language-action model that navigates virtual 3D worlds and completes hour-long objectives, alongside research on generative memory, focused attention for massive context windows, and latent steering of action experts. The company publishes its models and research code openly on GitHub.

providers.name: Planqc
providers.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Standard Intelligence
providers.description: Standard Intelligence (si.inc) is an aligned AGI research lab based in San Francisco building AI models that explore and learn like humans do. Its work includes hertz-dev, an open-source 8.5B-parameter autoregressive base model for interactive, full-duplex conversational audio; a fully general computer-action model that navigates websites, executes CAD sequences, and drives autonomously at 30 FPS; and The Heap, a 30-petabyte data-storage system built in San Francisco for under $500,000. The company has raised $75M from Sequoia and Spark Capital. It publishes research posts and open-source code on GitHub but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Authorea
providers.description: Authorea is a collaborative online platform for writing, editing, reviewing, and publishing scholarly and scientific documents. Founded in 2012 by Alberto Pepe and Nathan Jenkins, it lets researchers co-author articles in rich text or LaTeX, manage citations and references, embed data, figures, and code, run version-controlled review, and export to journal-specific styles. Authorea was acquired by Atypon in 2018 and is now operated as part of John Wiley & Sons, hosted on Atypon's Literatum publishing platform, where it supports preprints, journal submission, and open collaboration for the research community. It has no public developer API today; its earlier REST API was retired after the Wiley/Atypon acquisition, and the GitHub organization now publishes only document-processing tooling (LaTeXML, Pandoc, TeX styling) rather than API client SDKs.

providers.name: 9Slides
providers.description: 9Slides was a cloud-based presentation platform, founded by Ruchit Garg in 2011, that let users combine slide decks (PowerPoint, PDF, Keynote, Prezi, Excel) with synchronized video and deliver them through an HTML5 player viewable on desktop, tablet, and mobile. It operated on a freemium model, charging for premium features such as an ad-free player, password-protected presentations, and viewer analytics, and later pivoted toward learning and training. Backed by 500 Global, the company was acquired by employee-engagement platform Limeade. The 9slides.com domain no longer serves the product and now resolves to a parked/redirect landing page; no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

providers.name: Aemon
providers.description: Aemon is an autonomous AI research-and-development engineer founded in 2025 by Ray Xu and Richard Zhou and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Given an engineering problem and a measurable objective, Aemon reads state-of-the-art research, then generates, tests, and evolves thousands of candidate approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions that can exceed what human experts find. The team demonstrated the approach by setting a new world record on the NP-hard circle-packing optimization problem for under $10 of compute, beating a prior Google DeepMind result. Aemon is an early-stage, demo-first enterprise product headquartered in San Francisco; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: BlueLabs
providers.description: BlueLabs (withbluelabs.ai) is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building toward "emotional intelligence at scale." Its core technology, Blue-JST, is described as a novel dual reward mechanism designed to balance relationships and utility — an approach grounded in reward modeling and reinforcement learning. The company is backed by Forerunner Ventures and is actively hiring research talent. As of this profile it publishes a single marketing site (built on Webflow) with no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface; this record will be enriched as a developer- or agent-facing surface emerges.

providers.name: Cultivate
providers.description: Cultivate was an AI-powered digital leadership and coaching platform that analyzed leaders' own opt-in digital communication data to deliver hyper-personalized, privacy-preserving coaching insights and recommendations for people managers. Founded through an Entrepreneur in Residence program at Samsung NEXT by Joseph Freed, Samir Meghani, and Andy Horng, and backed by Trinity Ventures, Silicon Valley Data Capital, and Bloomberg Beta, Cultivate was acquired by employee listening and people-analytics company Perceptyx on February 15, 2022, where it became the basis for Perceptyx's "Cultivate Intelligent Coaching" product. Cultivate operated as an enterprise HR/leadership SaaS and did not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead record; the company no longer exists as an independent entity.

providers.name: Discovered Materials
providers.description: Discovered Materials (legally matforge inc) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) startup based in San Francisco building AI scientists for the semiconductor industry. The company uses swarms of AI agents to run the full materials-discovery pipeline - generating candidate materials, synthesizing them, and testing them in physical laboratories - to find novel materials for datacenters and fabrication facilities. Their stated goal is to compress a process that traditionally takes 10+ years of lab work into months, targeting 10x-better alternatives for applications such as nanoscale interconnects. Founded by Akash Ramdas (Stanford materials-science PhD/postdoc) and Advaith Sridhar (Carnegie Mellon AI, formerly Luma Labs and Persona AI). At the time of profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this entry is an enrichment lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Flourish
providers.description: Flourish (Flourish Labs) is a New York City based artificial intelligence research company building, in its own words, "human-level intelligence with human-level efficiency." Backed by GV (Google Ventures), the lab concentrates on advanced machine learning systems and foundational AI research rather than a public developer platform. At the time of profiling it publishes a marketing website but exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation, MCP server, or other developer surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio-lead stub and enriched with a live domain-security probe of its website host.

providers.name: GMR
providers.description: GMR (General Mining Research) is a crypto and Web3 company backed by Multicoin Capital and tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its public presence is a single-page web application at gmr.xyz identifying it as "General Mining Research" with a general contact at info@gmr.xyz. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, well-known discovery surface, or SDK/CLI could be found — the only machine-verifiable signal is the domain's TLS/DNS security posture. This profile remains a lead awaiting a published API or developer surface to enrich further.
